SARATOGA 200 KM BREVET DETAILS

Thank you for your interest in the Saratoga 200 KM Brevet. This ride is part of the Saratoga Brevet Series, and is sanctioned by Audax Club Parisien and Randonneurs USA, whose rules and regulations we'll follow.

Our usual route is a rolling loop through scenic Saratoga County, around the Great Sacandaga Lake and along the Hudson River. But, because 2011 is a PBP year, we may celebrate by creating a new route. Watch this space for more information.

Whatever route we use, be sure to dress according to the conditions, which can be tricky in late March. And, if you think you'll take more then 12 hours, you'll also need to bring your lights. To view our rider checklist, which has our minimum lighting requirements, click here.

We'll start riding promptly at 7 AM and will most likely start from the regional brevet manager's home at: 7 Pearl Street, Schuylerville, NY, or another nearby location. Please note that the regional brevet manager lives in a residential neighborhood, so if we use his home as the start, make sure to be courteous when arriving, departing and parking. For travel directions and parking instructions, click here.

This ride will be unsupported on the road, but services will be available at most checkpoints. We'll have food at the start and finish, along with Hammer Nutrition gels, drinks and bars to take along with us. We'll also have a small selection of lights, batteries, tires, tubes and other merchandise for sale at the start.

Same day registration will be available beginning one hour before start time.

To download an entry form, click here.

To download a cue sheet, click here.

For more information, or if you have any questions, feel free to contact us.

SPECIAL NOTES

The date is tentative and must be officially approved by RUSA in the fall. We don't expect any problems, but if it changes and a pre-registered rider can not make the new date, they will be given a full refund or credit towards another Adirondack Ultra Cycling event, whichever they prefer.

2011 is a PBP year, and if you are trying to qualify, you must be a member of RUSA beginning with the first brevet you intend to use to qualify.  If you need to renew, you may do so directly through RUSA or in person at any of our brevets.

ADIRONDACK 540 PREVIEW RIDE DETAILS


The 2010 one-lap, 136-mile, Adirondack 540 Preview Ride is scheduled for June 12.

It's held free of charge and is open to anyone, but is unsupported.

If you're planning on doing the Adirondack 540 RAAM Qualifier in September, this is a great opportunity to ride the course first hand with other ultra marathoners under friendly, non competitive conditions.  Even if you're not going to do the race, it's still a wonderful ride and is part of the Adirondack Ultra Challenge and the UMCA Year-Rounder Challenge.

The ride will start promptly at 7:00 AM. Please give yourself adequate time to arrive, sign in and get ready. Riders are expected to be on the start line at least 15 minutes before the start for last minute instructions.

We'll meet at the Alpine Country Inn and Suites, located at 5647 Route 86 in Wilmington. Their phone numbers are: 518.946.2263 or 877.946.2263, and they have generously offered to provide a room discount to any rider that needs overnight accommodations. For travel directions, click here.

Please note that this ride will be unsupported on the road. Services will be available on the route and are marked on the cue sheet, but riders should plan on being self sufficient. We'll have a sampling of Hammer Nutrition products, water and other drinks at the start, but there will be long stretches where services will be unavailable.

includes lodging [double occupancy; single supplement ($795.00) available],

TRIP HIGHLIGHTS
*Training in the beautifully scenic Limburg region of the Netherlands
*Training on the famed race climbs of the Walloon region of Belgium:
-Côte de la Redoute
-Côte de la Roche aux Faucons
-Côte de Saint-Nicolas
*Training on the famed race climb of La Flèche Wallonne, Mur de Huy
*Ride to and access at the following Professional events:
-Amstel Gold
-La Flèche Wallonne
-Liège-Bastogne-Liège
*In addition to spectating, riding, and site-seeing, this trip includes optional structured training with professional coaching!
*For a supplemental charge ($US295.00), entry into the Amstel Gold Amateur Cyclosportif with 6 course lengths from 65 km to the full 250 km of the Pro route

AVERAGE DAILY MILEAGE AND TERRAIN
We'll ride and train an average of 40-80 miles daily, over challenging terrain⎯bergs, cobbles, and narrow lanes. The routes are designed that you can do a shorter option or a longer option, and include areas where optional structured training can be employed. Professional coaching is included everyday. For those that want more, this cycling friendly region offers numerous roads to tackle after the set day's route.

WHAT'S INCLUDED
*Professional coaching, on-the-road clinics, and ancillary written or electronic training material.
*Experienced Rider Leaders and coaches. This is more than a tour; this is training with coaching.
*Daily detailed maps, route notes, and GPS files.
*Lodging in welcoming hotels.
*Cyclist-friendly breakfasts every day. Dinners are paid out-of-pocket for flexibility, but reasonably priced locations will be chosen.
*Full van support and snacks and drinks on the ride each day.
*Mechanical support.
*Transportation and luggage transfers during the tour.

WHAT'S NOT INCLUDED
*Airfare.
*Some non-van supported lunches are on your own, so you have maximum flexibility in your day.
*Dinners. We'll choose reasonably priced locations for those interested in group dinners.
*Bikes.
*Personal services, including laundry, telephone, hotel minibar charges, etc.
*Travel insurance.

April 14-19
State College Road Training Camp, State College, PA

The road riding in State College is phenomenal.  Phen-om-en-al.  Many of may know we've chosen this region of PA for Trans-Sylvania (www.TransSylvaniaEpic.com) - America's Most Fun Mountain Bike Stage Race Adventure - because of the incredible network of trails here.  Did you know that all those fantastic and beautiful mountains and hundreds of miles of paved (and dirt!) roads crisscrossing this lightly populated part of the state means the Alleghenies are just as spectacular a spot for a road focused training camp!  

State College is a fun place to visit too and we'll look to take advantage of all that Happy Valley has to offer.  Whether you're looking to prep for the race season or just get in a big block of incredible rides this is the camp for you.

Camp can be as much as 6 days, but we've structured this to make it as easy as possible for you to choose as little or as much of the camp as you can attend.  We have options of attending the camp from anywhere from 2-6 days and you may choose any combination of days you like - your camp does not have to start on Day 1 nor run concurrent days even.

Spring break starting on the 18th?  Join us from Sat to Tue!
Running into Holiday concerns during the second week of the camp?  Come up for Thur-Sat or Sun!
Want to race on Sat and/or Sun?  Make an awesome training block out of it and come out for Thur/Fri and then again on Mon/Tue!
That dang workin' thing getting in the way?  Just do Sat and Sun and maybe add on Fri too.
Want six days of awesome road riding goodness?  The whole camp is for you!!
We make it flexible so it fits your life and goals.

 

In fact, how can you pass it up? 

  • Incredible roads and climbs.
  • Flexible fee and days based on your schedule. 
  • Local.
  • Easy to get to and within a short drive.  
  • Inexpensive.  
  • Stellar opportunities to learn from highly experienced coaching staff.
  • Awesome town to hang out in after rides.
  • Fun!!

Bring friends.  Lots of them. 

You'll love it.  LOVE it. 

SAMPLE ITINERARY:

Day 1 - Start time 1:00PM so you have time to drive up in the morning to make this first day of camp.  Wake up the legs for camp with 40-50 miles of rolling central PA roads west of State College.  Likely to include some dirt roads too.  And probably a climb.  Yea, we'll climb.  On dirt.

Day 2 - Time for the real ups to begin as we head east from State College and tackle the gorgeous climb to Madisonburg and loop back through Bald Eagle State Park and Little Marsh Rd.  Figure on 70-90 miles today.

Day 3 - Rolling hills.  We'll head east from State College and enjoy the scenery and some pacelining along Penns Creek.  Then we'll rip back the valley while working on team time trialling for a fast trip back to State College.  You'll rack up about 65 miles today.

Day 4 - One of the best rides in PA awaits you as we tackle the biggest climbing day of the week.  This is our day to head north to Black Mo State Park and we'll hit four major climbs on today's route.  This one will be about 75 miles long.

Day 5 - This may end up as the longest day of the camp with a planned route of almost 100 miles including two long but gradual climbs that will be perfect for working on laying down the power.  Though long we'll dial down the intensity for this one except where those climbs beckon.

Day 6 - This is another fun one heading south from town taking in the Route 26 climb twice in a addition to a possible out-and-back at Greenwood Furnace.  We'll tune it up with some play racing and tactics practice on the roads between.  40-50 miles today wrapping up early so you can get home by dinner!

WEATHER CONSIDERATIONS

Weather in State College in April can be tricky, but overall it is pretty nice this time of year in Central PA.  In previous years we've run into rain one day of camp and temps in the low 50s to mid 60s.  No, it won't be balmy, but the training more than makes up for the need of arm and knee warmers and a rain jacket just in case (and, if we all carry rain jackets maybe we'll ward it off!).

Mountain Bike Endurance Race Camp

State College, PA (4 days, 3 nights)
MAY 12-15, 2011


Are you preparing to take on the challenges of the Trans-Sylvania Epic Mountain Bike Stage Race or another mountain bike stage racing event this summer?  Are you gunning for the summer NUE circuit or the MASS Endurance Series? How about Leadville or perhaps prepare for a solo assault on a 24 hour race? 


Four days of big rides and great training on the Trans-Sylvania Epic courses in State College, PA.  

This is a camp designed especially for YOU.


Trails that have been acclaimed as some of the best in the country await you in the Alleghenies while the camp is led by one of the most experienced mtb endurance coaches around - who happens to also be the head promoter for some of the best endurance mtb events going.  It is a perfect storm of making you fast. 


Scheduled two weekends before the start of the Trans-Sylvania Epic Mountain Bike Stage Race, this camp is an ideal way bring your fitness to a higher peak coinciding perfectly with start of the TSE.  As the training rides during this camp will all take place on TSE trails this is also a perfect opportunity to preview the exact courses on which you'll race.  Even if you're contemplating a run at the Trans-Sylvania Epic a year or more in the future this is a great way to test out the terrain and your mettle and learn from the best how to properly prepare. 


If you are not aiming to take on TSE our Power On Endurance MTB Camp offers an incredible opportunity to engage in a high quality block of training that will bring you to a higher state of readiness headed into the main thrust of the endurance race season.  The camp is perfect for the early summer 100s and 50s or for a good general preparation block for mid to late season long event.


Beyond four days of ideal training and absolutely incredible trails in the State College area you'll also receive instruction on the nuances of endurance mountain bike racing.  Not only will you hone your fitness you'll also learn how to best prepare for these kinds of events from physical, psychological, strategic and logistical standpoints. 


Organized and run by Mike Kuhn, coach to endurance racing luminaries like 2007 and 2008 US National 24 Hour Solo Champion, Rob Lictenwalner and Trans-Rockies podium finisher Ray Adams, this camp will bring your endurance mountain bike racing skills and knowledge to a higher level and teach you how to reach and exceed your goals.  Mike also offers his own experience gleaned from competing in endurance mtb races at the national level and more recent experiences stemming from preparing for competition while working long hours and after becoming a family man (yes, real life).  Additionally, as the originator and director of the Trans-Sylvania Epic there is no other person as uniquely qualified to prepare you for this particular event (he knows all the short cuts!) as Mike. 


Camp begins on Thursday at 2pm with a ride of the Trans-Sylvania prologue course.  On days two through four we will traverse the ridge top trails, long climbs and incredible descents in the Rothrock and Bald Eagle State Forests surrounds State College.  Camp includes a trip to Lake Raystown and the roller coaster like Allegrippis Trail network where we will work on high speed handling skills and preview this stage of TSE as well.  Evenings will offer opportunities to engage the coaches in discussions about endurance mtb competition and for recap of the days experiences.  You should expect each coach to offer not only general advice and guidance but also observations and suggestions specific to each individual who attends the camp.  Whether you're climbing, descending or slaloming the trees on the Allegrippis loop the coaches will be watching closely and offering you the benefit of their years of experience. 


You will come out of this camp a better and more complete mountain bike endurance racer and with a fitness boost to take you to a new level this year.

We're headed to Travelers Rest, SC for a week of excellent rides in the quiet hills and mountains north of Greenville.  We're timing this one for the end of Feb - perfectly placed for a big week in a late phase of your base training before the season starts rolling.  Camp will entail long rides to places like Caesars Head and perhaps even deeper into the Blue Ridge Mountains.  On at least one day you'll find yourself taking on the US National Championship Road Race climb on Paris Mountain.  Besides the great riding, Traveler's Rest is a very affordable place to stay and helps to make this camp a fantastic value.  With the relative proximity to many people and in the ongoing effort to make sure to fit the training I design to your life and your schedule you'll find a sliding scale of price based on the camp duration.  Of course, the full camp is great, but if you find a week long camp too long to be away don't let that stop you from making the trip!



From South Carolina Camp, Feb 2008.  Notice those short sleeves!  Nice!!

Register for the South Carolina Base Training Camp Today!!


Great riding.  Big climbs.  Warmer weather.  C'mon down.  Early pricing in effect through Jan 1.  Regular price after Jan 1, late fees after Feb 15 so get signed up!



SAMPLE ITINERARY

Day 1 - (Thu, Feb. 24) Travel to Travelers Rest* - Ride at 3:00 PM in Travelers Rest, basically until dark (bring blinking front and rear lights at minimum for the week).  We will traverse Paris Mountain, site of US Pro Championships in 2009 and 2010 at least twice today and maybe more. It will be a great way to shake out the legs from the trip and set the tone for an awesome camp.

Day 2 - (Fri, Feb 25) Long ride to mountains; includes climbs to Ceasars Head State Park.  The Greenville area climb.  Great going up with sweet switchbacks and an awesome view at the top.  And of course those switchbacks make it lots of fun coming down!

Day 3 - (Sat. Feb 26)  Long ride north of town into some cool real estate along a lake or two with winding roads and good but not super long climbing.  It will be a beautiful day on wonderful roads and a little break from the vertical challenges the rest of the week!

Day 4 - (Sun, Feb 27) Long ride (are you catching on to the theme?) with awesome dirt road section north of Travelers Rest; ride includes descent of Ceasar’s Head.  This is my favorite Traveler’s Rest ride I’ve found so far.  It is beautiful and the climb was not so bad you were dying but you got in some good vert!  Plus it is includes some good road bike dirt.  Sounds perfect, no?

Day 5 - (Mon, Feb 28) Today after breakfast we’ll hop in the cars and drive toward the Blue Ridge Parkway.  We’ll spend the day climbing up to; riding along and descending back down from one of the most beautiful roads in America.  Plan to be away from the hotel for basically the entire day as we will likely return after dark.  Bring extra clothes and gear!

Day 6 - (Tue, Mar 1) Last day of camp.  Please plan departures for later in the day if you can as we will hit up a short ride early and take on Paris Mountain one last time before you all jet off for parts unknown ready to kick some serious butt in 2011!


During the week we’ll be sure to make a few trips to Greenville to sample some local flavor and relax in the excellent downtown.  Traveler’s Rest also offers several places to eat and a few convenient shops within a short drive/walk/ride. 


Throughout the week we will take time to talk about cycling and multisports' multi-faceted challenges; from tactics to training to nutrition, mental prep and technologies like heart rate, power and gps, and more - you set the topic for discussion!

Maintain and build your cycling fitness through the winter.

Beat the cold, darkness, and the trainer doldrums this off-season.

Come train with Cycle Craft and Team Bulldog!


Although we don’t live in Vermont, the winters in our area can be tough for cycling.  And by the time you get home from work, there might not be much, or any, daylight left for you to get out and ride.  If you’ve ever ridden on a stationary trainer, you know it can be a great workout but can be mentally numbing.

Cycle Craft and Team Bulldog will be conducting trainer classes on Wednesday nights through the winter.  Each class will be 2 hours long (including warm-up and cool-down) and led by professional bicycle racer and coach, Brian Lariviere.  Two-thousand and ten was our inaugural year and we had great success.  The enthusiasm in the class was addictive, and the motivation levels stayed high.

This is a 10-week, structured class that builds over each session.  The two-hour workout is scripted by Coach B.L. and is designed to help you build endurance, leg speed, strength, and power while keeping it fresh and exciting.  We welcome beginners and experienced cyclists.

All you need is your bicycle (road bike or mountain bike with slick tire on the rear) and a stationary trainer.  It’s helpful, but not necessary, to have a heart rate monitor, cadence equipped bike computer, adjustable resistance trainer, and the ultimate training tool—a power meter.  Any of these items can of course be purchased at Cycle Craft to enhance your training experience.

For the ultimate in final touch preparation for the 2011 cycling or triathlon season, sign up for 24 sessions of leg-burning, lung-searing, wattage based workouts that will turn you in to a relative powerhouse among your peers.

The January - March training protocol starts off immediately hammering your Vo2 system, increasing efficiency and short-to-medium burst power. Then we'll actually take a step back and mix in some Threshold efforts along with the Vo2max stuff, and finally, in March, we'll go straight in to Motorpacing and race simulations. LOTS of anaerobic repeats, training your body to respond to the insane demands of road racing and short-course triathlon, as well as getting it to recover as quickly as possible, and prepare for the next heavy intervals. TXBRA racers, this program is perfect for your early season training and race preparation. Hills will seem easier, and you'll be better able to crack the peloton or bridge to breaks in the races in and around the Hill Country in early 2011.

This is not a USA Cycling race. this is better. With promoting as long as I have, I thought I was taken care of with insurance. Well I was wrong. If you take a look at all the other sports they all have insurance like USAC. So why does it cost so much? Why does it not cover you better? We looked into that and found out this. The promoter does not cover the rider insurance. The $3 the promoter pays is to protect everything else at the race. Riders are protected due to having a racing license. If you do not have health insurance you would have to pay a $5,000 deductable. For my April race I paid over $1,700 for this insurance though USAC. This year it only cost me $300. But this year I took out insurance to cover every racer in my race. It will only cost a $100 deductable. Both coverage cost me just over $600 this year.
 I have better Insurance for the riders and everybody else than what USAC can provide.  This race is what you except from a Norton type race. All the support you can ask for, and a great course.

WELCOME TO THE KILLER GRAVEL ROAD RACE

The third Annual BARRY-ROUBAIX March 26th 2011

Barry County Michigan

Presented by KISSCROSS EVENTS

Michigan's 2011 cycling race season kicks off this year with the Killer Gravel Road Race- The third annual Barry-Roubaix! Like the classic it's named after, Barry-Roubaix will test riders against rolling gravel roads (80%), pavement, one mile of rough two track, rocks, sand, mud, and possibly snow and ice, along with 2200 feet of climbing over its 35 mile loop.

What is Barry-Roubaix?

  • A classic road/off road race featuring a variety of terrain and surfaces to test all your cycling skills. Cyclocross, Mountain, Road, Single-Speed, Fixie and Tandem bicycles are all welcome. Road, mountain or cross bikes can be used in any category                 
  • The course will be determined according to conditions just prior to the race start. Maps will be available for pre-riding the course. Click on the map link on the website. The course will have three options and will be marked by colored arrows that match your number plate. Example: 23 milers will follow Blue arrows and 35/65 milers will follow Yellow arrows. (65's must complete 2 laps, not including 2 mile roll in/out). Course marshals will NOT be at every corner or intersection, rules of the road apply!
  • The course will NOT be closed to traffic and does not have a rolling escort. Cycling rules of the road apply, i.e. stop at all stop signs, yield to cars, no more than 2 riders abreast and do not cross yellow center line. Violations will be penalized by disqualification.
  • A sag van will make rounds looking for drop outs.

Where is Barry-Roubaix?

  • City-Middleville, Michigan
  • CourseBarry County
  • Start/Finish/Parking- Gun Lake Unit-Yankee Springs Recreation Area
  • Map: to start/finish area

Who is Barry-Roubaix for?

  • Cyclists and racers of all kinds and performance levels (no license required) that want to start their season with a real challenge and adventure  plus a lot of fun!
    • 65 miles (2 laps)*
    • 35 miles*
    • 23 miles*
    • Single Speed  23 miles or 35 miles*
    • Fixies (one brake mandatory)  23 miles or 35 miles*
    • Tandem- 23 miles or 35 miles*
    • * Distances are approximate depending on final course designation made prior to race start and we reserve the right to combine low category fields.
    • * Road, mountain or cross bikes can be used in any class. The 65 mile race is generally for elite/pro level athletes. Consider it is March, it may be cold out and last year it took the pros over 3 hours at 20+ mph avg!
    • Cut Off Time: For your safety no individual can start the second lap of the 65 mile race after 12:45 p.m.


What else can I expect at Barry-Roubaix?

  • $2000 cash awards, trophies and medals to the top three 65 Mile racers (no age categories). 1st-$500, 2nd-$300, 3rd-$200.  Michigan Youth Cycling and Kisscross Events will award $250 in scholarship to the fastest under 18 year old male and female in the 23 and 35 mile races each.
  • Trophies to the overall winner of the 35 and 23 mile race. Medals to the top three in age categories (age categories depend on the amount of registrations) and raffle prizes to many lucky racers. Podium awards and photos immediately following the completion of each category.

  • 4 wave starts (one for 65 milers, 2 for 35 milers, 1 for 23 milers)
    • Racers will be disqualified for starting in the wrong wave
  • Chronotrack Timing by Race Services Company. Rigid handlebar number plates with timing chips will be used for the best timing available.
  • All vehicles entering the Gun Lake Unit will need a Michigan State Park motor vehicle passport, either an annual or daily pass for $10. Out of state visitors can purchase a daily for $8 or an annual  for $29. Michigan residents please have permits purchased in advance to speed up the entrance to the parking area come race day. 



How do I register or volunteer for Barry-Roubaix?
  • You can pre-register December 15th, 2011 until March 23rd through BIKEREG.com

  • Want to get in free? Provide me with a volunteer for 2-33 hours. Contact me at amtnbiker@chartermi.net

  • Refunds are not allowed. If this is a transfer entry it will cost $5 and the exchange of the original entry fee is the responsibility of the two parties involved.
  • Friday registration (at Bay Pointe Inn from 3:00 p.m.-9:00 p.m.) or day-of registration (at the Gun Lake Unit from 7:30 a.m. and closes at 9:30 a.m.). These registration options are $10 additional

What:

Get ready for the ride of your life, The 6 Gap, as told by Bruce Saxton and as remembered by the late and great Chet the Jet Warman. I had the pleasure of accompanying Chet several times on this ride. It is a ride you will never forget and once you overcome the pain you'll want to do it again.  Riders will be able to choose between riding 2, 4, or 6 gaps.  Money raised from the ride will be dedicated to scholarships for aspiring young racers who can't afford a bike.  Nancy, Chet's sister, will manage the scholarship fund.

Course:

The Gaps are mountain passes located in Vermont's Green Mountains just north of the Killington/Pittsfield region and go as far north as the Sugarbush Ski Resort. The Gaps feature long steep climbs and twisting high speed descents. All 6 Gaps either start or end in close proximity along route 100. What you can expect:

* Approx. 132 miles riding distance and approx 14,000 feet of climbing
* Six mountain climbs ranging in 1300 to over 1900 feet net elevation gain
* A waterfall in the Granville Gulf
* Sustained grades of 20% to 24% on Lincoln Gap. "the longest, steepest stretch of road in America" Chet Warman
* Paved and some dirt road sections on both the climbs and descents
* Fantastic scenery, you'll feel like your in the tour at times
* You highest recorded speed if you dare
* Can throw in the towel after any combination of Gaps and head for the coffee shop
* A country store at the bottom of every gap, 2 bike shops along the way
* Great food and support during and after the event
* Cramps
 
Contact Chris Mitchell at: maltomitch@yahoo.com with any event questions.

MONTREAL DOUBLE DOUBLE DETAILS

Join us for a great ultra ride from Schuylerville, NY to Montreal and back.  This event is not a race nor is it a brevet.  It's something a little different.  It merges supported ultra marathon cycling with touring — a great combination!

Another Event? Am I nuts? Yes. I have a lot of fun with these holiday style races, so that's exactly what I'm going to do. This one will be inspired by a mental image of deranged easter bunnies on motorcycles.

The Easter Bunny or Easter Hare (sometimes Spring Bunny in the U.S.[1][2][3]) is a character depicted as a rabbit bringing Easter eggs, who sometimes is depicted with clothes. In legend, the creature brings baskets filled with colored eggs, candy and sometimes also toys to the homes of children on the night before Easter. The Easter Bunny will either put the baskets in a designated place or hide them somewhere in the house or garden for the children to find when they wake up in the morning.

Enduro is a form of motorcycle sport run on courses that are predominantly off-road. Enduro consists of many different obstacles and challenges. The main type of enduro event, and the format to which the World Enduro Championship is run, is a time-card enduro, whereby a number of stages are raced in a time trial against the clock.

This is not a real enduro, and we are not getting a visit from the easter bunnies. I am borrowing elements from both and morphing it into one unruly and exceptionally fun bicycle race/ride/thing. I'm going to use a lot of motorcycle terms that I don't fully understand to reference things because they have some obscure relevance, create alliteration, and are festive. This is supposed to be silly, ridiculous, and fun. Don't take it serious, but seriously consider doing it.

Scoring

This is where the enduro reference comes in. Your lap is timed, but it's not necessarily the fastest racer that wins. You get 1 point for every second that you are on course. You can pick up easter eggs on course to receive time bonuses. Eggs will be color coded. For example a blue egg might get you 5 seconds off your overall time and a yellow egg might get you 2 seconds off your overall time.

Example:
If you race the Hare and Hounds and finished in 10 minutes with two yellow eggs you would have a score of 596 points. If you finished in 10 minutes and 20 seconds and picked up 5 blue eggs, you would score 595 points. If you finished in 11 minutes and 2 seconds and picked up 12 yellow eggs and 12 blue eggs you would have a score of 578 points. Thus the last would be the winner. Fastest is not always fastest.

Primitive Camping at DirtFest

 

Please note all sites within Susquehannock peninsula will be used for tent camping only. If you wish to bring a camper or RV to DirtFest, or do not wish to camp inside the festival, please register as an off-site camper.  Susquehannock is considered a primitive campground, with on-site toilets, however it lacks shower facilities. Showers are available at the shuttle-serviced Seven Points Recreation area.

 

Individual Camping:

Details: This is the “general” camping category, for individuals, couples, and families which plan to attend the festival and tent camp inside the event on Susquehannock peninsula. This applies to registrants who do not have affiliation with a larger group (riding club, shop, etc.). Keep in mind you are not being issued an entire campsite, but rather a spot to camp within a larger group of other indivuduals. If you have several friends attending, please create a group name and register as a group to ensure you are put in the same place.

Parking: Somewhat limited. With fewer parking spaces than campers at each site, single drivers will be asked to unload their gear at the campsite, and relocate their vehicles to a shuttle-serviced parking lot. Cars will be parked within a short bike ride, but may not be directly adjacent to your campsite. Carpools will be given camp-side parking priority, and there is a shuttle available for all.

 

Grouped Camping:

Details: This applies to registrants who plan to attend the festival as part of a designated group.  Members of riding clubs, advocacy organizations, and groups of friends should register in this category.  As in years past, the size of a given group’s campsite will correspond with the volume of registrants. Parking: With the assumption that larger groups will travel in packs and carry more gear, some parking spots will be available at the campsites.  However, there is not enough room for every vehicle to stay in the camping area, so some will be asked to relocate to the shuttle-serviced parking lot.

 

Scud Package:

Our VIP package in homage to Scott Scudamore-the indispensable volunteer.  This category is for those who wish to show up early, help clean and ride the trails, enjoy the pre-event festivities, and generally lend a volunteer hand for the weekend.

Perks: Come early and stay late. Drink more beer. Help coordinate events. Set up tents. Free staff T-Shirt and other shwag. Not to mention some of the best sites in the campground. Contact us for more information if you are interested.

Day Visitors:

Off-Site Campers:

*NEW* Functional Threshold Power (FTP) Testing Class. Functional Threshold Power (FTP) is a key factor in your cycling arsenal. Don't worry if you have never heard of it.  Once you learn how it can enhance your workouts you will be hooked.  FTP is a function of the highest power output that can be maintained in a steady state for a period of time.    With so many regulars coming to the Speed Shop, it's time to offer another way to train even more efficiently.  During the last week of December look for a Functional Threshold Power (FTP) Testing Class.  The class is designed to determine your power zones in order to train more efficiently.    With a structured warm up, the test is done as a 20 minute time trial.  Once you have your appropriate power zones it allows you to apply them directly to each workout.  This is just another great piece of information in addition to heart rate and rate of perceived exertion (RPE).

The SpeedFreaks Stage Race is a 2 day, 3 stage Mountain Bike Race to be held on June 4th and 5th 2011. The event will be held on a private farm overlooking the Potomac River 3.5 miles north of Leesburg Virginia.

 This is a Solo event only and all competitors must complete all 3 races to be eligible for Awards.

 Race Caps: We will be capping the number of registrants for this race. SpeedFreaks will have 250 slots available for purchase, based on a first come, first served basis.

 Race Formats and Course Descriptions

 Time Trial: Saturday Morning. We will be having 2 Time trial courses this year. The Junior and Cat 3 racers will race the same 3.5 mile loop going through the "Pines" section of the course. Racers should anticipate times of 15-20 minutes. The Single Speed, Cat 1, and Cat 2 course will be using the trails on the back portion of the property. This will increase distance, time, and technicality. This will be a ~4.5 mile loop with expected times of 20-30 minutes. Both courses wil lbe running at sdame time, with racers starting every 20-30 seconds. Timing will be done using Go Time Racings RFID chip Timing system, so will be extremely accurate.

 Short Track: – Saturday afternoon. Races all afternoon on a .8 mile short track course laid out in the open so that Spectators can surround the entire course. The track has been layed out to utilyze the rolling hills and rock features of Rockland Farm to create a very fun, fast course. Most likely, Cat 3 and Junior racers will do 8 laps, Cat 2 and Single speeders will do 10 laps, and Cat 1 racers will do 13 laps. Goal is each race lasting about 30-45 minutes.

 Enduro: Sunday 3-5 hour(depending on category) Enduro race using the lengthened Leesburg Bakers Dozen course.The course is made up of rolling hills with plenty of semi-technical challenge in the form of rocks, roots, log piles, and small ledges. This is a fast course, but has been designed to accommodate all skill levels, from Beginner to Expert.   
 
Pre–Riding: There will be at least one, preferably 2 pre-rides, depending on Weather. Exact dates and times will be announced at a later date, please check back at this website. All participants will be asked to sign a liability waiver prior to pre-rides.

 Please note: The course is located on a private, active farm. The trails are closed to the public aside from race activities. In order to ensure future events and rides, please do not attempt to “poach” the trails prior to or after the event.

 Start Times: 

 Time Trial - Time Trial races will begin at 8:00am Saturday June 4. Racers will go off every 30 seconds. As we will be running concurrent races, Juniors & Cat 2's will start at 8:00 with alternating starts.  Single speeders, Cat 3's & Cat 1's will follow. Once we see number of entries, we will send out more exact start times.

 Short track – Short track races will start about 1 hour after last time trial finisher, and last all afternoon. We are unable to provide exact times until we see how many racers per category we have. Our goal is to have no more than 40 racers in each heat. We may combine categories to accomplish this. Conversely, we may also split categories into multiple heats, Example, if we have 75 Cat 2 Male racers, we will have two races, with finishing times establishing final placement.

Championship Point Series
 
The Championship Point Series (CPS) is Michigan's premier grassroots racing series.  The CPS raises funds to support local chapters in their ongoing advocacy work and trail improvements.  This race series attracts all levels of racers, from the first-timer to national and world champions.  These races are exciting and competitive, as well as beginner friendly for those wishing to try their first mountain bike race.  The CPS has been supporting races and racers twenty years.  The series is a unique collaboration between the MMBA chapters (as fundraising activities) and the Michigan's leading mountainbike race promoters.

Everyone is welcome to compete in any CPS race, but CPS points tabulations are reserved only for MMBA members.  Those who wish to be counted in the standings and eligible to win series awards can do so simply by joining the MMBA and then register here on BikeReg.com for their specific race category.  See the CPS rules for more information

ADIRONDACK 540 INFORMATION

The Adirondack 540 will be held September 17 - 19, 2010.  Our main event is the Adirondack 540 RAAM Qualifier, which will qualify riders for the 2011 - 2013 editions of Race Across America.

Race Headquarters will be at the Alpine Country Inn and Suites, located at 5647 Route 86 in Wilmington.  Their phone number is: 518.946.2263 or 877.946.2263, and they have generously offered to provide a discount to riders.

Our full race schedule includes:

Adirondack 540 RAAM Qualifier
Golden Gallop 408
Silver Sojourn 272
Bronze Blast 136
les Truffes Voyage 75/61

The centerpiece of the weekend is our beautiful and challenging 136-mile course.  Rolling hills, long climbs, thrilling descents and breath-taking views are a staple of this course.

Riders start in Wilmington, located 12 miles north of Lake Placid, right in the heart of the Adirondacks.  After a hilly jaunt to Lake Placid, riders keep climbing until the breath-taking descent into Keene.  Then it's a 4-mile climb out of the valley and southeast to Ticonderoga.

After passing through the second checkpoint, riders will travel north along Lake Champlain to Wesport, turn west through Elizabethtown and head back into the High Peaks region.

All races are non-drafting events (except the team competitions) and are officially sanctioned by the UMCA.  The Adirondack 540, Golden Gallop 408 and Silver Sojourn 272 are also part of the Ultracycling Cup.

Personal support crews are highly recommended, but not mandatory.

All events are sponsored by Hammer Nutrition.

All events are held rain or shine and entry fees are non refundable and non transferable.

All riders must be members of the UMCA.  One event and other memberships may be purchased in the merchandise section below, directly from the UMCA or at the race.

The 3rd annual AFC Sugar Hill XC Mountain Bike race will once again be held at the Avalon Area of Patapsco State Park in Elkridge, MD.

Half of the money made at this event will go towards funding the Extreme Weekend For Children with Diabetes camp for kids.  This camp is designed to help kids with diabetes learn how to manage their sugar levels while participating in physical activity.  It also provides a great opportunity for them to meet other kids who are going through the same things that they are.

The other half of the money raised will go to Kupenda for the Children.  Kupenda is an amazing organization that helps children with disabilities in Kenya.  They supply physical therapy, room/board at school, teachers pay, and a million other services that not only make a difference, but also saves lives!

Thank you for your participation!  We hope you have a blast at our race!!

Welcome to the 2011 Mid-Atlantic Super Series.

Racers wishing to participate in the series overall individual competition and MASS team competition must register for the series and pay a series fee of $25 for your primary racing class.  Racers wishing to race in more than one class will be able to register for additional classes for an additional fee of $5.00 for each additional class.  For example, if you are going to compete in the XC series competition and the endurance competition you will register for one of the classes and pay $25 and you will add the other class for $5.00.  Another example would be if you intend to race your age class at some races and singlespeed at other races.  Additional XC classes must be within the same XC category (Beginner, Sport or Expert/Elite). No USAC license required for MASS races.  MASS races follow a very generous payout schedule.   For more information visit www.masuperseries.com.
 
For 2011 racers will be issed a permanent number plate with timing chip attached to the back.  If you lose or forget to bring this to a race there will be a $10 replacement charge.
 
Season-end awards ceremonies will take place after the final XC race at the Bear Creek Mountain Resort.  Champions jerseys are awarded to every class winner.  Awards are given to the top three in larger classes. Smaller classes will just award a champions jersey. Team trophies are awarded to the top three teams in each team division.   There is no series fee for juniors.

EVENT RULES

-No littering. If I see you littering, I will kick you out of the event. This goes for gu wrappers and the like. Keep my forest beautiful.

-Be kind to everyone. NOBODY likes "that guy". Don't be that guy.

-If you cut the course, intentionally or not, own up to it. If you own up to it, I'll let you finish in last place of your category (it happens, I understand) and still earn points. -If somebody is hurt on course and you find them, it is YOUR responsibility to find a course marshal and let them know! No race is so important that you can't help someone out.

-No cheating, bad sportsmanship, throwing bikes, temper tantrums, uproarious behavior, or making a scene. I'll kick you out on principle.

-If you think there is an error in your results, bring it to my attention like a responsible adult. If you corner me and attack me about a finish error, I will kick you out and DNF you on principle. Nobody deserves that kind of behavior.

Location:  Samsung Austin Semiconductor, 12100 Samsung Boulevard, Austin, 78754

Please join us at Samsung for the 17th annual Rosedale Ride.  

Numbers are funny. One is 1-derful. Three is the charm. Nine is for revolutions, and 11 makes a football team. 16 is, of course, always sweet. But now there's Rosedale Ride 17. Can 17 really be sweeter than 16? Last year's weather was perfect, the roads were smooth, the rest stops friendly and the music toe-tapping, so it's going to be a challenge. But our planning is underway, we're feeling good, and we're hoping to make 17 even better than our most excellent 16. Samsung will, as always, graciously host. The volunteers are psyched. The roads are being checked and rechecked. Even the music is being booked as this is being written. We have a good feeling about 17.

The Rosedale Ride is an annual bike ride benefiting Rosedale School, the Austin Independent School District's only school for children with multiple disabilities. Open to cyclists of all abilities, the ride offers different courses to suit anyone. This year the Rosedale Ride has four courses to choose from: a Kid’s Fun Ride; or courses of 20, 43 or 63 miles. The ride begins and ends at Samsung, winding through the gently rolling countryside east of Austin.

This year, we are making changes to Package Pickup and the Silent Auction.  Put simply, we thought your visit to the School should be more fun. Wouldn't it be better if there was food and music to go along with walk-in registration? We thought so. So we're making it a celebration. We have contacted some fine restaurants and we have conscripted some excellent musicians and we're laying out the welcome mat right now. We're making the Silent Auction more fun and exciting, too. No more waiting until Saturday afternoon to see if you've won. Instead, we're accepting bids throughout the evening Thursday, then we'll close the bidding, and we'll distribute the goodies right there.

This will be a Thursday evening event only. Unlike years past, the School will not be open Friday for registration. This will give the staff some rest the evening before the Ride.

We hope you like our new approach. And we hope you'll come and bring your friends.

Community Center for the Blind and Visually Impaired invites you to the third Pedaling Paths to Independence on Saturday, February 26, 2011. A great ride for road, tandem, mountain, single speed, recumbent, high wheel, fixed gear, cruiser bikes, bikes Friday, and unicycles, the metric (67 miles with 1,300 feet of elevation gain) and quarter (25 miles with 300 feet of elevation gain) century routes begin and end at DeVinci's Delicatessen and Catering in Linden and traverse the quiet back roads of the San Joaquin Valley. Riders must be at least 16 years of age. All riders must sign a waiver upon check in at the event. Check-in will open at 8:30 a.m.; all riders must be on the road by 10:00 a.m. The course will close at 3:00 p.m.; post ride meal service will end at 3:30 p.m. Helmets are mandatory.
 
Fees ($40.00 for the metric century, $35.00 for the quarter century) include pastoral scenery, maps and route sheets, pre‑ride technical support provided by The Bicycle Café–Lodi, California, support and gear (SAG) vehicles, fully stocked rest stops, and a scrumptious post ride meal catered by DeVinci's Delicatessen and Catering Linden. Miles John Natural Light Photography will capture images of the event, which will be available for purchase.
 
A huge "thank you" goes to those who make Pedaling Paths to Independence happen: DeVinci's Corporation; Chris Trotter; Doug Beisner; The Bicycle Café–Lodi, California; Traffic Management Team, District 10, California Department of Transportation; The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Pacific Rim Branch; Tylor Coupe; Farmington Fire District; Keystone Lodge No. 161, Free and Accepted Masons of the State of California; Richard Freggiaro; General Mills, Inc., Lodi Plant; Roger Gray; Doug Keehr; Performance Bicycle Shop #55; Doug Ratliff; San Joaquin Lions Club; Stockton Bicycle Club; Stockton Delta Amateur Radio Club; Stockton East Water District; Rodney VanDunk, Mark Whitehouse, Clyde Zirbel. THANK YOU!
 
Community Center for the Blind and Visually Impaired has been lighting paths to independent living for more than 60 years. The agency provides specialized services to meet the rehabilitative, emotional, recreational, and social needs of individuals whose vision loss impedes the ability to perform tasks of daily living. THANK YOU for Pedaling a Path to Independence and allowing us to continue our work.

Learn the Skills to Get Faster Guaranteed!  With over 19 years of coaching experience including 12 years coaching downhill mountain biking Gene Hamilton knows how to get you riding at your best.  His coaching highlights include many top pro racers; Chris Van Dine, Mitch Ropelato, Joey Schusler, Eli Krahenbuhl, Chris Canfield, Naish Ulme as well as hundreds of riders and racers of all levels looking to reach their best. 
Dirt Magazine 2009 Pro 4x and Junior Cat 1 Downhill US National Champion Mitch Ropelato in an interview in the October 2009 issue:  
 
Interviewer: “You seem to be able to turn amazingly, what do you put that down to? Got any special tires on there?”

Mitch Ropelato: “Ya, Gene Hamilton is to thank for that, I took his clinic last December in Bootleg Canyon and he was able to show me the correct technique I needed to pull them off.”

 

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

The core fundamental skills of downhill mountain bike racing.  These core skills are not intuitive, unless someone taught you them it is unlikely that would know and understand them. Few US racers know the core skills and even fewer can do them well, which is the main reason we do poorly at the international level.  Through years of coaching and personal experience Gene is able to get the rider to understand these techniques with drills (that you take home with you for further practice and improvement) and then on trail application of the skills.  Get all the details and read student reviews at http://BetterRide.net

Indoor time trials (TT) provide some great off-season competitive bike racing. Riders race on their own bikes on one of twelve CompuTrainers. The riders feel exactly the same loads they would feel on the road at the same speed, grade and gear.
 
Riders in the Fast Splits Indoor Bike TT at Multisport World will line up side by side facing a large screen showing the course profile, each rider's position on the course, and each rider's race data including distance, elapsed time and power.  The Fast Splits Indoor Bike Time Trial is a 10k race for both teams and individuals with prizes awarded for the following:
  • 1st and 2nd Place Fastest Male
  • 1st and 2nd Place Fastest Female
  • 1st and 2nd Place Fastest Team
  • Random giveaways will also be distributed regardless of your time!
The TT will feature awesome prizes from supporting sponsors including Muscle Milk, Official Recovery Drink sponsor, and Rudy Project, Official Helmet sponsor of Multisport World 2011.  Prizes will include Muscle Milk cycling jersies and gym bags, Rudy Project TT helmets and Sport Mask USAT sunglasses and more. PLUS, the first 50 people who sign up for this TT will receive a Spinervals' DVD (a $30 value).   
 
TEAM PARTICIPATION: Teams enter with 4 members and the team's collective 4 times will count as the team's time.  The team with the fastest time will be crowned the TT champion. You save 15% by racing as a member of a team ($25) versus racing as an individual ($30) so grab some teammates, friends or training partners and compete together! PLUS... your team can race as part of the Champion System Team Challenge which consists of 3 competitive events at Multisport World: the Fast Splits TT, the Newton Running Campus Dash and the Relay Team Swim Challenge. CLICK HERE to learn more.
 
Please note, when registering your team you will need to have the birthdate and, for safety reasons, the name and phone number for all team members
 
WHAT TO BRING: Bike, bike shoes, water bottle, cycling clothes (team jersey if riding as part of a team).  Showers will be available to use at the TT, so bring a change of clothes and stick around to watch others participate and see who wins what!

About D2R2


The Deerfield Dirt-Road Randonnee was conceived in the 1990's as just a favorite dirt-road loop in the hilltowns of Franklin County, Massachusetts.  Since its birth as an organized event in 2005, many have hailed D2R2 as the hardest, most beautiful, most fun, most traffic-free, most unique, and overall best ride that they have ever done.  However, D2R2 will continue to maintain its original character as just a bike ride –

 

  • The courses will use the narrowest, oldest, twistiest, quietest, and most-scenic roads available.
  • A range of courses will provide access to novices as well as challenge the world's strongest riders.
  • D2R2 will never offer prizes for anything other than gags, nor will finish results ever be presented like it was a race.
  • Riders shall cover the course in a self-sufficient manner, without motorized crew vehicles.
  • The organization will put as much effort into its food offerings as it does the ride itself.
  • The event is a key fundraiser for the Land Trust's efforts to preserve land in the region, but the route sheets will always be available on its website for free.

Who is the Franklin Land Trust?  FLT is a 501(c)(3) devoted to the preservation of farm and forest land, and the rural character of western Massachusetts.  FLT helps farmers and other landowners protect their land from unwanted development.  To date, FLT has helped to preserve over 18,000 acres of open space.  The hills and valleys of the region—with their farms, sugar bush, rambling old New England roads, and small towns steeped in history—are a unique and precious resource which D2R2 riders will experience at every turn in the road.

The HPC Winter CompuTrainer classes are held at HPC, 783 Station Street, Herndon, VA 20170.
 
IF anyone has special requests for times - PLEASE let me know. If I have 6+ people who want a certain time I will add classes. This we are happy to do.
 
The first classes begin the week of January 10, 2011.
 
** It is recommended that if you plan on attending class twice per week that you sign up for either a Tuesday/Thursday OR Wednesday/Saturday combination. This will insure that the classes will offer variety and maximize your progressive training in the program.
 
There are 14 positions available for each class, sign up early!  Each class is 1 1/2-2.0 hours in length...arrive early, classes start on time. Many times the trainers will be empty (no previous class) and clients can come early to start warming up - if you like a longer warmup. The current block is 12 weeks in length.  Please bring cycling clothing, shoes, heart rate monitor, cadence sensor mounted on your bike, and plenty of hydration...be prepared to sweat and to get an awesome workout!
 
Questions? Contact Susan Hefler at shcoaching@verizon.net or Pierre Pelletier at pierrepell@yahoo.com

We will be doing another Functional Threshold Power (FTP) Test the first week of the class. So you will have current threshold power data. 
 
These classes run in a periodization fashion; meaning each class is built upon the last class. We will now be doing longer steady state and threshold type of training in the 2nd session. I will add in a Sunday class IF the weather is bad; this will go week to week and I will notify you all by email if we plan on having a Sunday class. 
 
Please email us for further information.

After a successful Road Camp in 2010, we are back with more in 2011! Both camps are 7 days and 6 nights with campers staying on the beautiful Miller School of Albemarle campus. From the time campers arrive until the time they leave, absolutely everything is provided for them.

Both camps include:
-3 healthy and balance meals each day
-Healthy snacks and ride food
-Daily fully supported group rides and skills courses led by area professionals
-Daily cycling seminars with topic ranging from nutrition and training principles to bike maintenance
-Laundry
-Bike mechanic

The Road Camp will feature rides on the the many small, winding roads that cover the surrounding area. We will also be riding on the scenic and challenging Blue Ridge Parkway several days. The area is far from flat, with many long, steep climbs, so plan your gearing accordingly! Also keep in mind that we will encounter short stretches of well-maintained dirt roads when making your tire choices (23mm 'training tires' will be more than adequate). While the road camp is for all levels of junior riders looking to improve, it is important that all participants have previous experience, and are comfortable, riding in a group.

We are also happy to announce the CBC Road Camp will serve as a Talent ID event for the Colavita/Baci Elite Junior cycling Team. Top performing riders from the camp could earn a spot on the roster for the 2012 edition of the Tour de l'Abitibi, one of the premier Junior stage races in the world.

The Mountain Bike Camp will showcase some of the best trails on the East Coast. We will ride all of the Charlottesville area staples such as O Hill and Walnut Creek; but then also venture over the Blue Ridge Mountains and shred Sherando Lake and Douthat State Park, among others.

There are also quite a few options to keep everyone entertained when off the bike. The Miller School of Albemarle campus is outfitted with everything you could ask for in the middle of summer, including:
-Swimming pool
-12-acre lake
-Canoes
-Basketball courts
-Tennis courts
-Baseball fields
-Soccer fields

We can assure you there will never be a dull moment!

*With camps running back-to-back, campers attending both camps are welcome to go home for the night in between, or stay on the Miller School of Albemarle campus. There are meals and activities planned for those campers who stay.

*Please contact us if you may need airport pickup. We will be able to facilitate pickups from the Charlottesville-Albemarle Airport (CHO) only.

details: Join us for an epic day of cycling on the back roads of Bedford County and the Blue Ridge Parkway.  The Storming of Thunder Ridge English & Metric Century will challenge your mental and physical readiness with over 9,000/6,000ft of climbing, including a 13 mile climb (Thunder Ridge) to the summit of Apple Orchard Mountain – a noteworthy climb that boasts an average 5% grade.  When asked about Thunder Ridge, the 1994 Tour du Pont winner, Viatcheslav Ekimov stated, “It is long, but not very steep”.  The roads leading up to the climb are moderately rolling hills surrounded by beautiful scenery.  The 35 mile option (Foothills of the Blue Ridge) follows the same roads except it eliminates the route on the Parkway – it rolls along the base of the mountains through Curtis – and then rejoins the metric route for the last fourteen miles.  All three routes promise great support, quiet country roads, and breathtaking views.  The ride will be followed by music, food, massage and fun!

Crazy Magic 12 & 6  hour Trail Ultra Run

Sunday, August 14th

9am- 9pm
Get a team formed, or go solo!

Weather: race will be held rain or shine. Expect highs in the 90's, am temps in the 50's. If severe thunderstorms roll in, we will stop race until past, or call race if needed, standings at that time will be official results.
 
Restrooms: The park has limited restrooms that are located about ½ mile away from the race site. There is also a porta potty at the soccer fields about ¼ mile from race start. We are not supplying any port johns of our own..so pea in the woods…but if yu have to do number 2….decide in advance where you would like to go! Sorry!!

Food/ Aid: You will pass by the log in tent approx. 5 miles each time,  we will have limited water, power drink and food. Make plans to bring what you or your team requires for this event, use our food as back ups. 

Results: Awards will be presented asap after the last runner comes in. There will be a 10 minute protest period, and then we will begin, we hope to be presenting by 9:30pm

 
Prizes: We will be giving away some great prizes to the winners. All Merchandise Prizes, and all great stuff. Prizes will be three deep in each field.

T SHIRTS FOR SALE OF $5, order BY July 22, GET A SPECIAL EVENT TSHIRT!

Starts 9am , Mass Style Start ,then race your heart out for 12 or 6 hours.
Whoever does the most laps wins!

Course Description: Technical 5+ mile loop, in centralpark, schenectady. Course is almost all singletrack. Roots, rocks, bridges, logs, steep up and down hill. For a link to the trail information go here: http://capitalmtb.org/Resources/Schenectady%27s_Central_Park_Trails.
Unlike most Ultras, this course has allot of twisty turns, prepare your knees for the impact.

Pit area/ log in & out:There will be an open pit area, neutral station for aid. In this area will be the registration table, log in  & out form lap area, a feed station. We will also have a runner row, in which each person or team will have an assigned spot for pop up tent, food, chairs, ect.
The pre race meeting will be held in the log in/ out tent.

Rules:  A duo or three person  team must have each runner on the course for a alloted amount of time, meaning one runner can run 50% of the time, and the other runner must run 30%- 20% of the time. There will be no course cutting allowed.
 Any  runner who cuts course will be DQ, along with the rest of their team. 

Race Start/ Finish: The format of the event will be a mass start, it is the participate in each catogory who completes the most laps in 12 hours. Runners must check out from their final lap after 6pm, no crossing the line until 6pm, or you must do another lap. 
. 
Check in and pick up Number between 8:30am- 8:45am. Prerun meeting at 8:50am.

The Beezley Burn is a fun filled mountain bike festival that has become a fixture on the Northwest cycling calendar.  The weekend kicks off Saturday with the fast paced action of short track racing at Oasis Park followed by the Vicious Cycle free BBQ and tent camp out.  Sunday morning is the infamous Beezley Burn cross country mountain bike race which has become well known for the grueling course and prize give-away that follows.  Not to mention the top pros from all over Northwest coming to battle for the $2000 pro pay-out, this is one weekend of cycling you don't want to miss.

Bring the whole family for some awesome, spectator friendly racing.
PRO/OPEN will race for 20 min. all other classes will race for 15 min.  Come and enjoy the Vicious Cycle BBQ following the Final race.  Free tent camping!

Indoor time trials (TT) provide some great off-season competitive bike racing. Riders race on their own bikes on one of eight laboratory matched CompuTrainers. The riders feel exactly the same loads they would feel on the road at the same speed, grade and gear.
 
Riders in the Amaiza Fitness Indoor Bike TT at Multisport World Conference and Expo will line up side by side facing a large screen showing the course profile, each rider's position on the course, and each rider's race data including distance, elapsed time, and power.  The Amaiza Fitness Indoor Bike Time Trial is a 10k race for both teams and individuals with prizes awarded for the following:
  • 1st fastest MALE: Time Trial helmet from Rudy Project
  • 2nd fastest MALE: $50 gift cert provided by Bonzai Sports
  • 3rd fastest MALE: $25 gift cert provided by Bonzai Sports
  • 1st fastest  FEMALE: Time Trial helmet from Rudy Project
  • 2nd fastest FEMALE: $50 gift cert provided by Bonzai Sports
  • 3rd fastest FEMALE: $25 gift cert provided by Bonzai Sports
  • 1st Fastest TEAM: Time Trial helmet from Rudy Project for all three members
  • 2nd fastest TEAM: $25 gift certs to all three members of the team from Bonzai Sports
PLUS, the first 50 people who sign up for this TT will receive a Spinervals' DVD (a $30 value).  ALL participants -- whether signed up as a member of a team or as an individual -- will be eligible to win the Fastest TT for their gender. 
 
TEAM PARTICIPATION: Teams enter with 4 members and the team's collective 4 times will count as the team's time.  The team with the fastest time will be crowned the TT champion. You save 20% by racing as a member of a team ($20) versus racing as an individual ($25) so grab some teammates, friends or training partners and compete together! Please note, when registering your team you will need to have the birthdate and, for safety reasons, the name and phone number for all team members PLUS... your team can race as part of the Champion System Team Challenge which consists of 3 competitive events at Multisport World: the Amaiza Fitness TT, the Newton Running Campus Dash and the Relay Team Swim Challenge. CLICK HERE to learn more.
 
WHAT TO BRING: Bike, bike shoes, water bottle, cycling clothes (team jersey if riding as part of a team).  Showers will be available to use at the TT, so bring a change of clothes and stick around to watch others participate and see who wins what!
 
WHERE AND WHEN: The Amaiza Fitness Indoor Bike Time Trial is a part of the Multisport World Conference and Expo held at the Hanley Center for Athletic Excellence at Georgetown Prep in North Bethesda, MD. The Time Trial takes place right on the expo floor and you choose the time of your heat when registering.

About 70% changed from 2010.  No busy highways, no steep climbs, but plenty of rolling hills to keep it interesting.  The pavement ranges from smoot h new asphalt to typical rural chipseal.  Rugged wheels and pie-plate granny gears won’t be needed.  All routes will be sag patrolled, rest stops (five on the 101) will be about 15 - 20 miles apart and have drinks, snacks and restroom access.  A post-ride meal and hot showers will welcome you back to the park.  Grab a bite and then wind down with a mountain bike ride! 

Bring the family- Bike widows & orphans can enjoy the park’s many attractions while they await your return – including the country store, crafts cabins, water-driven grist mill, cotton gin and many other 1800’s buildings, miniature railway, hiking & biking trails, picnic & camp grounds, Iron & Steel Museum, and, of course, the historic blast furnaces.

40 mi - Helena ‘n’ Back ~1100’ el. gain  
Riders will again take country roads out to the first rest stop near Helena, then mostly backtrack (with an interesting variation) as they return to Tannehill.

73 mi - Pea Ridge Ramble ~2600’ el. gain  
Riders will cross the Cahaba and head south, then turn west for the gradual climb to the route’s high point at Pea Ridge.  After a rest stop at Bart’s BBQ & Country Store, the return to Tannehill passes the “castle” at Marvel along a very rural route through the Cahaba River Wildlife Management Area, as riders re-cross the river and take a final rest stop near West Blocton before the last push home. 

101 mi  - Ironworks Century ~3500’ el. gain 
   * BBC Tour de Iron Butt Stage *
Before taking the Ramble route back to Tannehill, the Ironworks 101 rolls down off Pea Ridge to wind around the town and University of Montevallo (with a rest stop on the veranda at Eclipse Coffee & Books).  Riders will then pass by the American Village historical exhibition en route to reprising their Pea Ridge ascent and revisiting Bart’s BBQ.

Want to have more fun on the trails? Want to be more efficient and mountain bike with more confidence? Still find yourself hoping to make some corners, getting nervous in tight switchbacks or feeling lucky, not skilled after that technical section?  Gene Hamilton and the certified BetterRide coaches know how you feel, because they have all been there.  Gene was held back in his professional racing career by the same fears and lack of proper technique that most riders experience.  But that was before BetterRide…

Gene has designed a comprehensive skills training program that continues to prove itself as the best in the US.  BetterRide coaching sessions will help you with both the mental and physical sides of mountain biking. The goal is to help you reach your potential by teaching you the core skills of mountain biking and the drills to master these skills. These are the non-intuitive skills that keep mountain bikers of all levels from reaching their potential. Learning and becoming proficient at these skills will allow you to ride in balance and in control making you a more efficient and confident rider.

Starting in a safe learning environment BetterRide certified coach Dylan will explain then demonstrate the skill and have you practice the skill utilizing drills that you will continue to use long after the camp. Once you understand the skills we then apply them on the trail. At BetterRide Gene and his coaches truly enjoy helping riders progress and would love to share these techniques and the drills for practicing, getting good at and eventually mastering these techniques with you. This is the most fun and informative mountain bike school you will ever attend!

The Stockton Bicycle Club invites you to its thirty‑third Delta Century. Bucolic Jessie’s Grove Winery again will host the event that traverses the rural Delta roads of the San Joaquin Valley. Flat quarter (26 miles, zero elevation gain), metric (62 miles, 260 feet of elevation gain), and full (100 miles, 425 feet of elevation gain) century loops cover scenic vineyard, farm, and Delta roads–and a ferry ride across Steamboat Slough (metric and full century routes only)–with rewarding rest stops along the way. You’ll commemorate completion of your Delta Century ride on the beautiful grounds of Jessie’s Grove Winery with a delicious post ride meal catered by DeVinci’s Delicatessen and Catering Lodi and entertainment by Creative Sounds DJ and Sound Services.

   Proceeds from the Delta Century benefit local charities. Riders, sponsors and volunteers helped the Stockton Bicycle Club donate a record $12,000.00 to the following organizations in 2010: Amador County Team Policing Bikes for Kids Program; Animal Friends Connection Humane Society; Arthritis Foundation; Calaveras County Sheriff’s Volunteer Unit; Community Center for the Blind and Visually Impaired; Emergency Food Bank; Galt Assisted Learning and Enrichment Program; Delta Chi Chapter, Gamma Phi Beta Sorority; Horizon Church Mission 360 (M360) Ride; Jenny Lind Veterans Memorial Building Fund; Library and Literacy Foundation for San Joaquin; Lodi Cancer Kids; Lodi House; Make-A-Wish Foundation; New Hope School District; River Delta Unified School District; Rocket Sports Foundation; Sacramento County Regional Parks; Salvation Army, Lodi; Salvation Army, Stockton; Shriners’ Hospitals for Children‑‑Northern California; Stockton Delta Amateur Radio Club.
 
   Fees include pre-ride technical support by The Bicycle Café—Lodi, California (visit www.LodiBicycleCafe.com to learn more about the shop), detailed maps and route sheets, great food and drink along the routes, support and gear (SAG) vehicles, a scrumptious post ride meal catered by DeVinci’s Delicatessen and Catering Lodi, entertainment by Creative Sounds DJ and Sound Services, and the gracious hospitality of the Stockton Bicycle Club. Miles John Natural Light Photography will capture images of the event, which will be available for purchase.

   Check in will open at 6:00 a.m. for the full century, 7:00 a.m. for the metric century, and 8:00 a.m. for the quarter century. All riders must be on the road by 9:00 a.m.; the course will close at 4:30 p.m. Riders still on the course will be asked to SAG to the finish; those who refuse must complete the ride on their own. The post ride meal will be served between 11:30 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.

   Riders younger than 16 years of age must be accompanied by an adult registered for the ride. All riders must sign a waiver at the event. Each rider must wear an ANSI or US CPSC approved helmet, ride single file, and obey all traffic laws. Earphones, headphones, ear buds and similar devices are prohibited. Bicycles should be in good operating condition. Each rider should carry a minimum of a spare tube, patch kit, bike pump or cartridge, cell phone, money, identification, water bottle.

   Gratitude and appreciation go to those who help make the Delta Century happen: Jessie’s Grove Winery, The Bicycle Café-Lodi, California, Richard Carli, New Hope School District, Old Sugar Mill/Carvalho Family Wines, Performance Bicycle Shop #55, River Delta Unified School District, Sacramento County Regional Parks, Stockton Delta Amateur Radio Club, Vellum Cycles. THANK YOU!

• SEASON PASSES: Men's and women's season passes work out to paying for one race per night for 25 weeks, meaning you receive 7 weeks at the Driveway for free. It's a great deal if you are able to race more than one category each week and participate often.
    • FINE PRINT: Season pass holders enjoy a separate and expedited registration line, no additional race fees, and if you lose your season pass card, we can replace it. Season passes are non-transferable. No refunds.
  • PUNCH CARDS: This is designed for the regular participant on a budget or the regular participant who because of their category and age cannot race more than once per night (i.e. 34 and under in age and a Cat 1 or 2). If you participate often, but not enough to warrant the purchase of a season pass, the punch card is for you. Weekly rates apply (i.e. additional race fees, etc) but you use the card at your leisure. Think of it like a pre-paid credit card but for the Driveway, and by pre-paying you basically recieve a 10% discount ($200 in credit for $180). When you run out of credit, buy more! 
    • FINE PRINT: The punch card is transferable, meaning you can use it to pay for a buddy if you want. Unfortunately because of the transferable nature, if you lose it, we cannot replace it for you or provide you with a refund, it's simply lost or being used by some lucky person who found it! We suggest writing your name with a sharpie on the back of the card. Punch card holders use the regular line at registration. 
  • IMPORTANT! PLEASE READ - Punch Cards and Season Passes do not guarantee you a spot at the races. Every week races are first come first serve and they do fill up. There is no pre-reg. Last year the Cat 4/5 race sold out 9 times! The 3/4 and P1/2/3 races came within 2-3 people of selling out a half dozen times last year and we anticipate that they will sell out this year several times. Please take that into account when purchasing a season pass or punch card. If you are a Cat 4 or Cat 5 and think you're going to barely make it to the Driveway in time for your race often, especially in the opening months, you may want to reconsider a Season Pass purchase as you'll find that the 4/5 race is often full. If you're stuck on the sidelines, we apologize, but we can't offer you a refund or pro-rata refund on your season pass purchase.

The Maine Time Trail Series
 
The Maine Time Trial Series races will take you to 12 fantastic venues all over the State of Maine from Presque Isle to Mt. Agamenticus, Fryeburg to Bar Harbor and many places in between.  This year, we have added some new events that are sure to be both challenging and rewarding. 

The Series is open to everyone, whether you are a highly talented racer or a recreational cyclist entering the competitive scene.  Time trialing is a perfect opportunity to try your hand (and legs) in a bicycle race.  No pack riding, so it's a perfect venue for first time competitors.  You do not need a special time trial bike to participate in our races, you only need the bike you have.  Riders are started at 30-second intervals, and it is just you against the clock.

This year, we are offering 12 races with the final race, the State Championships, worth double points (scores).  In order to qualify for series prizes, riders must race in a minimum of 4 races.  Riders will accumulate points for each race they compete in with their top 8 scores counting towards their overall score.  The better you place, the more points you receive, and the male and female with the highest points at the end of the season will receive the highly coveted perpetual trophies.  In addition, top placers in all divisions will win prizes at individual races as well as at the year-end celebration.  We will also offer fabulous raffle prizes at all the individual races and at the end of year, thereby giving all participants a chance to win regardless of how fast you are.

Along with the commitment of the Bicycle Coalition of Maine, we are fortunate to have so many of our state's local bike shops sponsoring and supporting these races.  Most races will have on-site bike mechanical support at the start line, the support being provided by each race affiliated local bike shop.  Our race directors and their teams of dedicated volunteers work hard to ensure the courses are safe and the races are well run -- and fun events. 

The Maine Time Trial Series is a unique and outstanding series of races in all of New England.  Join us for the thrill of competition, the chance to win wonderful prizes no matter how well you place in the race, an opportunity to support the Bicycle Coalition of Maine's superlative advocacy efforts in Maine, and a chance share great cycling tales and adventures with fellow enthusiasts.

Rules

Helmets are required to be properly worn, with the strap buckled, at all times on the bike whether warming up, racing, or cooling down (riding trainers excluded).

No headphones or ear buds may be worn by racers on or near the race course during warm up, race time or during cool down (riding trainers excluded).

Starting order is chosen by order of registration, random selection, or numerical order.

Each racer shall report to the start line at least three minutes before his or her scheduled starting time and shall be prepared to start at their scheduled time.  If a racer appears later than the scheduled starting time, the racer may come to the start line and must come to a complete stop – no flying starts are permitted.  He/she may not interfere with those starting on time, and it will be up to the discretion of the starter when the late starter may start.  His/her start time will be recorded as their scheduled start time, not when they actually do start.  By missing their start time, the racer forfeits their chance to restart and may not schedule a new start time.

Starting times will be at equal intervals, typically 30 or 60 seconds.

The racer shall be held by a volunteer or official at the start, but shall neither be restrained nor pushed.  No restarts are permitted.  It is permissible to start with one foot down if the racer so desires.

Racers are to follow Maine State Law and bicycle safety rules and shall ride as far to the right as practicable except when passing.

Races are held on open courses – racers ride with traffic and are solely responsible for their own safety at all times.  At no time are racers allowed to endanger traffic or the public.
Racers are bound by the local traffic laws, unless a police officer or other authorized person directs you to take otherwise illegal actions (such as passing a stop sign).
Passing must be done on the left only – no passing is allowed on the right, ever.  Passing racers must give adequate room so as to not endanger the racer being passed.  Calling out is strongly encouraged when passing.

Drafting is strictly prohibited.  Racers must be at least three bike lengths behind the bike ahead.

No two racers may ride abreast other than when one is attempting to pass the other.

No support vehicles or parking are allowed on the course.

The Race Director is allowed to make additional rules provided they are within reason and explained to everyone before the start of the race.

Failure to abide by any of these rules is grounds for disqualification.  Registration in any of the Maine Time Trial Series serves as acceptance of these rules as they are posted on the Maine Time Trial web site and available at each race. 

The Race Director’s decision in all matters is final.

Important things to note: your bike must have breaks, your jersey must have sleeves, you can't wear a jersey with a team logo unless you are a member of that team.
