ADIRONDACK 540 INFORMATION

The Adirondack 540 will be held September 17 - 19, 2010.  Our main event is the Adirondack 540 RAAM Qualifier, which will qualify riders for the 2012 - 2013 editions of Race Across America.

Race Headquarters will be at the Alpine Country Inn and Suites, located at 5647 Route 86 in Wilmington.  Their phone number is: 518.946.2263 or 877.946.2263, and they have generously offered to provide a discount to riders.

Our full race schedule includes:

Adirondack 540 RAAM Qualifier
Golden Gallop 408
Silver Sojourn 272
Bronze Blast 136
les Truffes Voyage 75/61

The centerpiece of the weekend is our beautiful and challenging 136-mile course.  Rolling hills, long climbs, thrilling descents and breath-taking views are a staple of this course.

Riders start in Wilmington, located 12 miles north of Lake Placid, right in the heart of the Adirondacks.  After a hilly jaunt to Lake Placid, riders keep climbing until the breath-taking descent into Keene.  Then it's a 4-mile climb out of the valley and southeast to Ticonderoga.

After passing through the second checkpoint, riders will travel north along Lake Champlain to Wesport, turn west through Elizabethtown and head back into the High Peaks region.

All races are non-drafting events (except the team competitions) and are officially sanctioned by the UMCA.  The Adirondack 540, Golden Gallop 408, Silver Sojourn 272 AND Bronze Blast 136, are also part of the UltraCycling Cup.

Personal support crews are highly recommended, but not mandatory.

State College Road Training Camp, State College, PA

The road riding in State College is phenomenal.  Phen-om-en-al.  Many of may know we've chosen this region of PA for Trans-Sylvania (www.TransSylvaniaEpic.com) - America's Most Fun Mountain Bike Stage Race Adventure - because of the incredible network of trails here.  Did you know that all those fantastic and beautiful mountains and hundreds of miles of paved (and dirt!) roads crisscrossing this lightly populated part of the state means the Alleghenies are just as spectacular a spot for a road focused training camp!  

State College is a fun place to visit too and we'll look to take advantage of all that Happy Valley has to offer.  Whether you're looking to prep for the race season or just get in a big block of incredible rides this is the camp for you.

Camp can be as much as 6 days, but we've structured this to make it as easy as possible for you to choose as little or as much of the camp as you can attend.  We have options of attending the camp from anywhere from 2-6 days and you may choose any combination of days you like - your camp does not have to start on Day 1 nor run concurrent days even.

Spring break starting on the 18th?  Join us from Sat to Tue!
Running into Holiday concerns during the second week of the camp?  Come up for Thur-Sat or Sun!
Want to race on Sat and/or Sun?  Make an awesome training block out of it and come out for Thur/Fri and then again on Mon/Tue!
That dang workin' thing getting in the way?  Just do Sat and Sun and maybe add on Fri too.
Want six days of awesome road riding goodness?  The whole camp is for you!!
We make it flexible so it fits your life and goals.

 

In fact, how can you pass it up? 

  • Incredible roads and climbs.
  • Flexible fee and days based on your schedule. 
  • Local.
  • Easy to get to and within a short drive.  
  • Inexpensive.  
  • Stellar opportunities to learn from highly experienced coaching staff.
  • Awesome town to hang out in after rides.
  • Fun!!

Bring friends.  Lots of them. 

You'll love it.  LOVE it. 

SAMPLE ITINERARY:

Day 1 - Start time 1:00PM so you have time to drive up in the morning to make this first day of camp.  Wake up the legs for camp with 40-50 miles of rolling central PA roads west of State College.  Likely to include some dirt roads too.  And probably a climb.  Yea, we'll climb.  On dirt.

Day 2 - Time for the real ups to begin as we head east from State College and tackle the gorgeous climb to Madisonburg and loop back through Bald Eagle State Park and Little Marsh Rd.  Figure on 70-90 miles today.

Day 3 - Rolling hills.  We'll head east from State College and enjoy the scenery and some pacelining along Penns Creek.  Then we'll rip back the valley while working on team time trialling for a fast trip back to State College.  You'll rack up about 65 miles today.

Day 4 - One of the best rides in PA awaits you as we tackle the biggest climbing day of the week.  This is our day to head north to Black Mo State Park and we'll hit four major climbs on today's route.  This one will be about 75 miles long.

Day 5 - This may end up as the longest day of the camp with a planned route of almost 100 miles including two long but gradual climbs that will be perfect for working on laying down the power.  Though long we'll dial down the intensity for this one except where those climbs beckon.

Day 6 - This is another fun one heading south from town taking in the Route 26 climb twice in a addition to a possible out-and-back at Greenwood Furnace.  We'll tune it up with some play racing and tactics practice on the roads between.  40-50 miles today wrapping up early so you can get home by dinner!

WEATHER CONSIDERATIONS

Weather in State College in April can be tricky, but overall it is pretty nice this time of year in Central PA.  In previous years we've run into rain one day of camp and temps in the low 50s to mid 60s.  No, it won't be balmy, but the training more than makes up for the need of arm and knee warmers and a rain jacket just in case (and, if we all carry rain jackets maybe we'll ward it off!).

HUNTER ALLEN - PEAKS COACHING GROUP POWER CAMP

Training and Racing with a Power Meter Spring Camp

Bedford, Va  April 3 -9th, 2011

 

Rising out of the Blue Ridge Mountains, two prominent peaks stand out against the sky giving Bedford one of the most beautiful backdrops in Virginia. Part of the Blue Ridge Parkway, these peaks are known as The Peaks of Otter and act as the backdrop and challenge of the Peaks Coaching Groups premier cycling camp.

 

Join Hunter Allen, Scott Moninger and the Peaks Coaching Group for this six day cycling camp in the scenic Blue Ridge Mountains.  Based out of Peaks Coaching Group headquarters, this camp offers cyclists the ability fine tune their foundation training and prepare for the upcoming season while exploring the Valley's and Peaks of Southern Virginia and the Blue Ridge Parkway.

         Daily Power Training Seminars and on-the-road coaching from Hunter Allen

         Advanced Power Training Techniques and WKO Utilization methods that will improve your results

         Low traffic road and miles of training on the Blue Ridge Parkway

         Learn from and train with Scott Moninger to get those inside the peloton tips

         One-on-one coaching and power file analysis from Hunter, Scott and the rest of the Peaks Coaching team

         Fully supported rides featuring on the road coaching, key training drills, power testing and great camaraderie.

         Catered evening meals and lunches

         Post ride yoga sessions

 

The Cost for the Camp will be $1,799 per person and will include lodging and all the other great things mentioned above.  Lodging will be in the local Days Inn Hotel (subject to change), double occupancy. It will cost extra if you want a private room for the duration of the camp ($250).  Transportation to and from the airport is included.

 

Nearest Airport: Lynchburg Regional Airport

Lodging: Days Inn, Bedford, VA (included)

 

Target Athlete

This will be an intermediate/advanced camp for racers and fast recreational riders who have been training for 1 year or more, and/ or are Cat 4 and higher. We highly recommend bringing your power meter and laptop to get the most out of these camps but are not mandatory. Rides will be from 60  90+ miles each day, with shorter options if needed. Please email Hunter Allen at info@peakscoachinggroup.com if you have any questions as to the suitability of this camp for you.

 

Camp Fee

$1,795 (Double Occupancy, $195 additional for single occupancy).  The camp fee includes all coaching, six nights lodging, 6 breakfasts, 5 lunches and 5 dinners, fully supported rides, mechanical support, gels and bars

 

Camp Itinerary

Will be supplied in camp information packet.

 

Camp Accommodation*

Conveniently located Bedford, Va, Days Inn is the ideal location to call your home away from home, be it business or pleasure, offering:

       Complimentary wireless Internet in public areas

       Complimentary parking

       Internet access in every room - nominal fee applies

                              *subject to change

 

Arrival & Check-In: Sunday, April 3rd, 2011

Check-In begins at 3:00pm Sunday afternoon, dinner that night is on your own but there is an 8:00pm riders meet & greet.

 

Meals

Breakfasts provided by hotel.  Lunches & Dinners will be catered and/or supplied by the hotel or local restaurants. Sunday night dinner is on your own based on arrival times and is not included in the package pricing.

 

Weather

Spring weather in Bedford tends to be mild.

 

Airport Shuttles (from Lynchburg Airport)

We have airport shuttles available from Lynchburg Airport. Please contact us as soon as you know your travel arrangements so we can book pickups.

 

Departure: Saturday, April 9th, 2011

Please allow 1 hour for the drive plus check in time at the airport.

 

Bike Shipping:

Bikes can be shipped in advance and will be held for your arrival.  We will supply specific shipping address in camp information packet.

 

Camp Cancellation Policy:

The total camp fee minus $150 is refundable for withdrawals up until Jan 25, 2011. For withdrawals after Jan 25, 2011 but on or before February 8, 2010 50% of your full camp fee payment is refundable.  For withdrawals on or after February 8, 2011 no refund will be made available.

» About the NEBC Introduction to Bicycle Racing program

 

As it has every Spring since 1993, the Northeast Bicycle Club is offering its Introduction to Bicycle Racing program to the public during the month of April, 2011. This 4 week program will introduce you to the exciting world of bicycle road racing, and will prepare you to enter and be competitive in your first race. Among the things you will learn are:

  • Bike handling: Cornering; pacelines & double pacelines; riding in close groups; incidental contact.
  • Racing skills: Sprinting; time trialing; climbing and descending; starting and finishing.
  • Tactics and strategies: Road racing as a team sport; applying team strategies and tactics in race situations; using the race course and your strengths to your advantage.
  • Training and equipment: Periodization and specificity; training effort zones; racing bicycles & equipment; maintaining and performance tuning your equipment; proper bike fit.

At the conclusion of the program is a Graduation Exercise, in which we will bring you to an actual race to test out your new skills!

 

» 2011 Schedule

 

Evening classroom sessions:

Location: Burlington Public Library, Burlington, MA
Dates: Wednesday March 30th and Monday April 11th, 2011
Time: 7:00pm – 8:30pm

Saturday morning riding sessions:

The NEBC Introduction to Racing program consists of 2 evening classroom sessions and 4 Saturday morning riding sessions. The classroom sessions will cover fundamental information on bicycle racing and training. The riding sessions will concentrate on riding and racing skills and drills. The graduation exercise is an actual USCF race, for students to put to use what they have learned.

The year 2011 Introduction to Bicycle Racing program is by pre-registration only. The series is designed as a progressive program, with each new skill building upon the foundation of the previous skills. Due to the limited time available, it is difficult to make up missed sessions, so please be able to attend all sessions.

 

» What You Will Need

 

  • A road bike in good working condition. Cyclocross or mountain bikes with smooth tires may be allowed by permission (no knobby tires or handlebar extensions!).
  • An ANSI or Snell approved helmet.
  • Adequate clothing for weather conditions – the riding portions of the clinics go on rain or shine (because races do too!).
  • A good attitude and a willingness to try new things!

 

» Cost

$45 for non-licensed Riders.
$25 for riders holding a USA Cycling License.
$25 for Jr Racers (must be 18 or younger by 12/31/2011)

About the Grand Fundo:

In the cycling world, a granfondo is a massive group ride / race, sometimes thousands of riders, encompassing all levels and abilities, from pros to tourists. We have titled this ride a Grand Fundo because it will be grand and more fun than any granfondo.  The Fundo is not a race, it's 64 miles and the course includes approximately 20 miles of dirt roads. No rider will be left behind, rest stops will be provided along the route, lots of support riders and a follow car with spare wheels and a mechanic.  Following the Fundo, we'll retire for music, a bonfire and a pig roast which we hope you will enjoy with us.  

J.A.M. is a fund created by Jeremy Powers, Alec Donahue and Mukunda Feldman.  Good friends, brought together because of a passion for cycling over ten years ago.  The goal of J.A.M. is to help motivated, young cyclists to reach their potential both on and off the bike, all while not being limited by finances.  This will be reached through close mentoring and involvement in the cycling community.  Grants will be issued to young cyclists in and around the Pioneer Valley who show the interest, determination, and desire to be their best.  It's also our goal to showcase the amazing cycling that the pioneer valley offers. So all entry fees will go directly to the J.A.M fund.  We look forward to seeing everyone there!

About D2R2


The Deerfield Dirt-Road Randonnee was conceived in the 1990's as just a favorite dirt-road loop in the hilltowns of Franklin County, Massachusetts.  Since its birth as an organized event in 2005, many have hailed D2R2 as the hardest, most beautiful, most fun, most traffic-free, most unique, and overall best ride that they have ever done.  However, D2R2 will continue to maintain its original character as just a bike ride –

 

  • The courses will use the narrowest, oldest, twistiest, quietest, and most-scenic roads available.
  • A range of courses will provide access to novices as well as challenge the world's strongest riders.
  • D2R2 will never offer prizes for anything other than gags, nor will finish results ever be presented like it was a race.
  • Riders shall cover the course in a self-sufficient manner, without motorized crew vehicles.
  • The organization will put as much effort into its food offerings as it does the ride itself.
  • The event is a key fundraiser for the Land Trust's efforts to preserve land in the region.

Mountain Bike Endurance Race Camp

State College, PA (4 days, 3 nights)
MAY 12-15, 2011


Are you preparing to take on the challenges of the Trans-Sylvania Epic Mountain Bike Stage Race or another mountain bike stage racing event this summer?  Are you gunning for the summer NUE circuit or the MASS Endurance Series? How about Leadville or perhaps prepare for a solo assault on a 24 hour race? 


Four days of big rides and great training on the Trans-Sylvania Epic courses in State College, PA.  

This is a camp designed especially for YOU.


Trails that have been acclaimed as some of the best in the country await you in the Alleghenies while the camp is led by one of the most experienced mtb endurance coaches around - who happens to also be the head promoter for some of the best endurance mtb events going.  It is a perfect storm of making you fast. 


Scheduled two weekends before the start of the Trans-Sylvania Epic Mountain Bike Stage Race, this camp is an ideal way bring your fitness to a higher peak coinciding perfectly with start of the TSE.  As the training rides during this camp will all take place on TSE trails this is also a perfect opportunity to preview the exact courses on which you'll race.  Even if you're contemplating a run at the Trans-Sylvania Epic a year or more in the future this is a great way to test out the terrain and your mettle and learn from the best how to properly prepare. 


If you are not aiming to take on TSE our Power On Endurance MTB Camp offers an incredible opportunity to engage in a high quality block of training that will bring you to a higher state of readiness headed into the main thrust of the endurance race season.  The camp is perfect for the early summer 100s and 50s or for a good general preparation block for mid to late season long event.


Beyond four days of ideal training and absolutely incredible trails in the State College area you'll also receive instruction on the nuances of endurance mountain bike racing.  Not only will you hone your fitness you'll also learn how to best prepare for these kinds of events from physical, psychological, strategic and logistical standpoints. 


Organized and run by Mike Kuhn, coach to endurance racing luminaries like 2007 and 2008 US National 24 Hour Solo Champion, Rob Lictenwalner and Trans-Rockies podium finisher Ray Adams, this camp will bring your endurance mountain bike racing skills and knowledge to a higher level and teach you how to reach and exceed your goals.  Mike also offers his own experience gleaned from competing in endurance mtb races at the national level and more recent experiences stemming from preparing for competition while working long hours and after becoming a family man (yes, real life).  Additionally, as the originator and director of the Trans-Sylvania Epic there is no other person as uniquely qualified to prepare you for this particular event (he knows all the short cuts!) as Mike. 


Camp begins on Thursday at 2pm with a ride of the Trans-Sylvania prologue course.  On days two through four we will traverse the ridge top trails, long climbs and incredible descents in the Rothrock and Bald Eagle State Forests surrounds State College.  Camp includes a trip to Lake Raystown and the roller coaster like Allegrippis Trail network where we will work on high speed handling skills and preview this stage of TSE as well.  Evenings will offer opportunities to engage the coaches in discussions about endurance mtb competition and for recap of the days experiences.  You should expect each coach to offer not only general advice and guidance but also observations and suggestions specific to each individual who attends the camp.  Whether you're climbing, descending or slaloming the trees on the Allegrippis loop the coaches will be watching closely and offering you the benefit of their years of experience. 


You will come out of this camp a better and more complete mountain bike endurance racer and with a fitness boost to take you to a new level this year.

1-All sites within Susquehannock Campground Peninsula will be used for grouped tent camping only. Individual: Grouped Camping: $40.00 Pre-Registration or $50.00 Day Of
Details: This applies to registrants who plan to attend the festival as part of a designated group.  Members of riding clubs, advocacy organizations, and groups of friends should register in this category.  As in years past, the size of a given group's campsite will correspond with the volume of registrants.  Smaller clubs may be grouped together sharing one site. Of course the clubs that bring the most members ultimately get the coolest sites....waterfront.
Parking: With the assumption that larger groups will travel in packs and carry more gear, some parking spots will be available at the campsites.  However, there is not enough room for every vehicle to stay in the camping area, so some will be asked to relocate to the shuttle-serviced parking lot.

Details: This is the general camping category, for individuals and  couples,  which plan to attend the festival and tent camp inside the event on Susquehannock peninsula. This applies to registrants who do not have affiliation with a larger group (riding club, shop, etc.). Keep in mind you are not being issued an entire campsite, but rather a spot to camp within a larger group of other indivuduals. If you have several friends attending, please create a group name and register as a group to ensure you are put in the same place. This means if you have a group of four or more register with a group name, to ensure you camp together. As one of the ideas behind the weekend is building a larger rider network.....be positive it's sure to be a good time.
Parking: Somewhat limited. With fewer parking spaces than campers at each site, single drivers will be asked to unload their gear at the campsite, and relocate their vehicles to a shuttle-serviced parking lot. Cars will be parked within a short bike ride, but may not be directly adjacent to your campsite. Carpools will be given camp-side parking priority, and there is a shuttle available for all.

Capacity: 4-10 (depending on size of boat)

As part of a DirtFest weekend special Seven Points Marina is offering free weekend passes to the event and 20% off seasonal specials to all clubs or groups renting a houseboat.

Our VIP package in homage to Scott Scudamore-the (in)dispensable volunteer.  This category is for those who wish to show up early Wednesday, help clean and ride the trails, enjoy the pre-event festivities, and generally lend a volunteer hand for the weekend. You will be called upon when its raining, told to clip poision ivy, and asked to clean out the inside of Scuds tent. Perks: Come early and stay late. Help coordinate events. Set up tents. Free staff T-Shirt and other shwag. Not to mention some of the best sites in the campground. Contact us for more information if you are interested. Or sign-up and see what happens.

The Lehigh Valley has experienced substantial growth in recent years, and as a consequence, the area has experienced a significant loss of farmland (nearly 4 square miles every year). In order to reduce further loss of our prime farmland to development, we need a new crop of farmers who can operate profitable farms in a way that protects and enhances the natural resources of the rich farmland we have here in the Lehigh Valley.

To protect and preserve our farmland and agricultural heritage, Lehigh County has created an agricultural incubator project called the Seed Farm, which is helping to train new farmers to establish new sustainable enterprises in the region. The Seed Farm, located on a 25 acre site in Upper Milford Township, will help ensure a source of healthy food for residents and revitalize the economy by facilitating the growth of a vibrant local food system.
 
To help promote the Seed Farm and its mission, the Lehigh County Farmland Preservation Program is holding the 3rd Annual Sowing Seeds Charity Bike Ride on Saturday, August 27th starting at the Lower Milford Township Park.  We hope that the event will not only raise funds to help establish the Seed Farm, but also engage the community and increase the visibility of local farmers.  Routes of 20 and 40 miles are available  and farm fresh food will be served to reward participants.

REGISTRATION:
Register on line.  We expect the race to sell out prior to each event.  Please register early as we are limited the number of total racers to 100!  Once we reach that number we will close registration.  There will not be prizes for each race, but we will have prizes for series points after the Sept. 21st race!  

SWAG:  All series entries will receive a 2011 event pint glass and other swag... tbd.  One glass per person for the series.

DISTANCE:
All races will be about 45 minutes.

NUMBER OF LAPS:
After one lap the number of laps of the race will be determined.

LAPPED RIDER:  
If you are lapped you can continue to race.  Once the leader finish all remaining riders will complete their current lap and then finish.  It will be scored by number of laps completed then time.

DONATION:
Donations will go to the local trail working groups (MORE/Friends of Forest Hill Park) earmarked to maintain the trails at Forest Hill Park.  Please donate a few bucks during registration.

Dragon's Tale 2011 - Epic Route 40 Miles - Scenic Tour 20 Miles

The Tale of the Dragon is a long one versed with history. It began with Kyle Inman's "Dragon's Back" in the late 1990's. The unique backcountry singletrack event brought some amazing racing to trails not often used in mountain bike events. Tight, narrow, mossy, off-camber Appalachian sidehill singletrack that run's a tight and rocky spine like ridgeline. It's a wonder that the bicycles of the 90's were able to complete the course. Not only did they complete the course, but "they" included world famous riders like Flyod Landis, Jeremiah Bishop, Gunnar Shogren, Sue Haywood, Carol Waters and Chris Eatough. This new generation of the event uses the same great core loop of Kyle's forever popular "Dragon's Back" event less the Turkey Trail downhill with the bonus "tail" added on that climbs and descends Broad Run Mountain and then gives a memorable run in on Ferrier Trail to finish along Craigs Creek next to New Castle, VA. Craigs Creek is a tale for another day.
 
This event is made possible with the generous support of East Coasters Bike Shop in Roanoke and Blacksburg, Just the Right Gear in Roanoke, Blue Ridge Bicycle Club, Pathfinders for Greenways, and the honorable Jeff Cheng, Ben Brown and Kirby Walke. Permitted by the Jefferson National Forest.

Come Experience riding the Blue Ridge Parkway ... 

Join your friends and fellow cyclists in the breathtaking Blue Ridge Mountains of Central Virginia on Sunday, May 22 for the second annual Storming of Thunder Ridge road ride.

This well-supported event offers camaraderie and challenge for every rider’s ability with a choice of 35, 65 and 100 mile routes as you ride at your own pace along safe and scenic well-marked country roads.

The 35 mile route follows a challenging course of rolling hills and meandering back roads. A longer 65 mile route tests rider stamina with a 13 mile ascent to Apple Orchard Mountain, the highest peak of the Blue Ridge Parkway in Virginia. For an epic day in the saddle, the 100 mile route boasts over 9000 feet of climbing.

Your registration helps fund the Community Support Campaign of the YMCA of Central Virginia. Included are cue sheets, fully stocked rest stops, mechanical support and monitoring of riders along the course.

One of the most respected women in mountain biking has joined the team of BetterRide certified coaches. Join retired professional racer, Sue Haywood for this two day camp that will cover the BetterRide training curriculum with drills and on trail practice.  For more information please send an e-mail to gene.hamilton@betterride.net
 
 
Sue Haywood's Bio:
Sue started riding mountain bikes in the wild woods of West Virginia in

1991.  She did her first beginner race that year finishing second out of

two in the beginner class. Even though she wasn't very good,  she liked

it. She went on to race  the West Virginia Series(WMBA) for the next

seven years and eventually turning pro in 1998.  In 1999, she became a

member of the Trek/Volkswagon Racing Team with distinguished teammates

like Alison Sydor, Roland Greene, Travis Browne and Wade Bootes.  Her

career highlights include 3 Short Track National Championships, I Super

D National Championship, 2 World Cup Podiums, 1 24 Solo World

Championship, Winner of La Ruta, Trans Rockies, Pisgah Mt. Stage Race

and the Shenandoah 100.

 

She now considers herself a recreational pro dabbing in select races

that she thinks are cool and special.  She brings to Better Ride years

of racing, training and teaching experience.  She loves to ride big

rocks and wet roots on an epic day.  But she also loves seeing students

gain confidence in their riding abilities and having lots of fun

learning new skills.

Course Info: Course Map
The Morgantown Road Race is bringing back the famous 2009 course!! If you want to climb your legs off come join us over in West "by god" Virginia/Pennsylvania for some wicked hard yet truly fun road racn'!! This course starts and finishes at historical Mason Dixon Park on Buckeye Road. This race course has just about everything a cyclist could wish for in ridge top views, back country road, big climbs and gear pounds flats. Starting out at Mason Dixon Park you head West to wards Blacksville then head North on rt 218 into Pennsylvania. Ride 218 all the way up to Waynesburg. A quick right on cook road and over top the mountain you will find yourself returning south on Sugar Run Road. At Kirby, PA take a right on Kirby road and then it back country roads all the way back to the finish at Mason Dixon Park.

 Voted top 10 hardest race courses in America!


Course: View a copy of the Course Map 
Mountain Top Finish in the heart of the Mon National Forest! Leave your expensive Flux-Capacitors and fancy wheels at home cause it's WV and we got pot holes, but do not forget your climbing legs, and yes, they can have hair on them too. We don't judge! Be prepared to climb with this course. Cat 1/2/3 and Cat 3/4 will see three large climbs over 7 miles long. All other classes will face two large climbs of 7 miles in length. This course also takes you along the Cheat River for several miles of wonderful view of the mountain state. The course will features a mountain top finish on Sugarlands Road. This climb has one of the largest grades in the entire county. The start of this race will happen at Tucker County High School, but for safety reasons there will be a controlled roll to the bottom of Sugarlands Land for the start. This will give riders who didn't get a chance to pre-ride the course a good view of the finishing climb. Once at the bottom of the mountain the race is on. The Cat 4/5, Cat 5, Masters, Juniors and all Women's Classes will do one loop of the course "view course map". The 1/2/3's  and 3/4's will have to do the climb at location two times before returning to the Sugarlands road.

Course Info:
You can bring your fancy wheels for this one but do not forget your climbing legs, and yes, they can have hair on them too. We don't judge! This course is 59 miles long taking you through the mountain valleys of WV and ridge tops.  This course has tons of long flat section(really more then any other ABRA event) along with two long stead climbs to remind you that this is a Appalachian Bicycle Racing Association event. Also these roads are in the nicest shape of any seen all year on the ABRA circuit so break out the deep dish carbon wheels for this one. This course starts and finishes along side the beautiful Cheat River in Rowlesburg, West Virginia and  has just about everything a cyclist could wish for in a bike race along the way.  Beautiful river views, streaming descents, big climbs and gear pounds flats.

Info:

Join World T.E.A.M. Sports this April 15-17, 2011 for our annual Face of America bike ride to honor our military—disabled, veterans and active duty—and the true America Spirit.

The ride kicks off in our Nation’s Capitol with a festive banquet before embarking on a 110 mile journey to historic Gettysburg, Pennsylvania. Face of America is much more than a bike ride, it is an opportunity to share stories and build camaraderie with over 400 other participants.

Face of America is one of our nation’s few truly inclusive bike rides and continues to change the way the world views injured and disabled athletes

EVENT DETAILS

On April 16 & 17, World T.E.A.M. Sports will host the 2011 Face of America Bike Ride, an annual two-day bike ride from our Nation’s Capitol to Gettysburg, to honor and assist our military — disabled, veterans and active duty — and the true American Spirit.

This inspiring ride is an opportunity to welcome  servicemen and women who are disabled, and able-bodied servicemen and women, as teammates and show them how much we appreciate their efforts. We will also have the opportunity to show them that they can still be a part of the TEAM.

Registration for civilian riders is $100, retired military $50, active duty $50, Wounded Warrior participation is FREE.

This registration fee includes Friday night dinner, Saturday breakfast & lunch, Sunday steak and beer at the ride finish and return bus transportation from Gettysburg to Washington, D.C.

Fundraising minimums for 2011 are:  civilian riders $750, retired military riders $500, active duty military riders $250. Wounded warriors are not required to fundraise for this event, but are encouraged to do so.

To be eligible to participate in the ride, every participant will be required to pay the balance of his or her fundraising goal at final ride registration the night of April 15. Funds raised through event registration and donations support our events and disabled athletes participating in our events.

The Kick-off Dinner Friday night at the Hyatt Regency Washington is included in the registration fee. Participants can purchase additional dinner tickets for their guests online at the time of initial registration for $35. Guest tickets are $40 if purchased the night of the dinner on site.

The ride will travel approximately 55 miles each day, with an overnight stop on Saturday in Frederick, Maryland. Lodging and dinner for Saturday is the responsibility of each participant. World T.E.A.M. Sports has secured rooms and special event rates at hotels in Frederick.

RIDE LOGISTICS

World T.E.A.M. Sports has arranged with the Hyatt Regency Washington, a short distance from the start of the ride, to allow riders to leave their vehicles in valet parking on Friday, Saturday and Sunday at the discounted rate of $25 per day. THE NATIONAL RIDE OF SILENCE -- A VOICE THROUGH SILENT PRESENCE

On May 18 2011, at 7:00 PM, the Ride of Silence will begin in North America and roll across the globe. Cyclists will take to the roads in a silent procession to honor cyclists who have been killed or injured while cycling on public roadways. Although cyclists have a legal right to share the road with motorists, the motoring public often isn't aware of these rights, and sometimes not aware of the cyclists themselves.

The Ride Of Silence is a free ride that asks its cyclists to ride no faster than 12 mph and remain silent during the ride. There is no brochure, no sponsors and no registration fees. The ride is held during Bike Safety month which aims to raise the awareness of motorists, police and city officials that cyclists have a legal right to the public roadways. But most importantly, the Ride is an opportunity to show honor and respect for local cyclists who have been killed or injured while cycling...please come & and be a part of this special event!

WHY THE RIDE OF SILENCE?

-  To HONOR those who have been injured or killed
-  To RAISE AWARENESS that cyclists are here
-  To ask that we all SHARE THE ROAD

It's time to ride in the RAW.  Come support the Brushy Mountain Cyclists Club by riding in our longest running event.  We'll mark 18 years straight with these great routes.
 
25 Mile Route

The 25 mile route loops through the rolling hills south and east of Wilkesboro, offering views of the Brushy Mountains and the Blue Ridge.  No long climbs, but there are plenty of shorter hills to test your mettle. The 25 mile route has a rest stop midway.  

40 Mile Route

The 40 mile route is a loop with a scenic out-and-back section midway.  Test your early season form on two challenging climbs to Windy Gap, the route's high point. Fill your need for speed with two daring descents. The RAW 40 features two rest stops: one at the foot of the Windy Gap climb and a second at the turn-around point at the Old Jarvis Store.

65 Mile Route

The 65 miler winds through the fields, forests and orchard country of rural Wilkes, Iredell and Alexander Counties while still climbing the two marqee climbs, Windy Gap and Brushy Mtn Road..  

The RAW 65 crosses the spine of the Brushy Mountain range twice, putting you to the test on two tough climbs:

Anne Arundel County, Maryland

Minimum field of 30 riders in all field except for: Women’s senior open field which has a 21 rider minimum and the Women’s 4 field which has a minimum of 10 riders. The Juniors’ fields have a minimum of 10 riders for each age category.

 

Race Category Cancellation: The Race Promoter reserves the right to cancel any race that has less than the minimum field after online registration closes. Races that are cancelled may be replaced with a field from the wait list.

 

Racer Sign In: will occur at Race Headquarters at Southern Middle school,
5235 Solomons Island Road, Lothian, MD.  Sign-in opens at 7:00 am and
closes 30 minutes before each event.

 

***Riders who register on the appropriate BikeReg Wait List will be allowed to

register on the day-of-race if spots are available within 30 minutes of the start.
 

Course: The course is run on a 6.75 mile rolling, smooth road circuit in Anne Arundel County, Maryland a short drive south from the City of Annapolis.

 

All races will start at the school and proceed to the race course as a neutral rolling start.  The race will start on Bayard road (Rt 422) and will proceed clockwise taking a right on Polling House Road, a right on South Polling House Road and right back onto Bayard road. 

 

The centerline rule will be in effect and strictly enforced for the entire race including the neutral start. For the final 200 meters of the race racers will have access to the full width of the road.

 

All applicable traffic laws are to be obeyed when traveling from the finish area to the school and outside the confines of the race convoy.
 

The finish line will be on South Polling House Road on a short 12% uphill slope just prior to the intersection with Bayard Road.

 

A separate cash prize of $20.00 “aggressive rider sprint” will be awarded to the rider who wins the aggressive rider sprint on each lap prior to the finishing lap. There will be no aggressive rider sprints in the Juniors fields.

 

Feed Zone: In the Pro, Cat1,2.3 race only the uphill grade leading to the area adjacent to the golf course will be used for the feed zone. Pro, 1,2.3 racers may feed on laps 6 and 7 only.  Race marshals will mark the feed zone accordingly for support personnel to distribute food and refreshments. Riders may not discard material that is not biodegradable; riders may pass or throw such material to support personnel on places far from bystanders. Support personnel leaving the feed zone area should return to the registration area via driving in the opposite direction of the race.
 

All USA Cycling Rules Apply: Event will be held rain or shine. If unlicensed, Cat 4 Women and Cat 5 Men (including Juniors of the same categories) are the only categories that can purchase a USA Cycling One Day License in order to race (available at the event for $10.00).

 

Junior Gearing Roll Out: For all junior riders (including senior races) gear restrictions will be enforced. Roll out of all junior rider bikes will be performed prior to the race as a courtesy. Post race roll out for juniors is required. This applies to juniors racing in Men’s senior fields as well. The Chief Referee will preannounce the roll out time and location on race day (check with day-of sign in desk for more information on the roll out location).

 

MABRA BAR Scoring: Men’s Cat 4/5 and Men’s Cat 4/5 35+ are not MABRA BAR

events. Other events will be eligible for the MABRA BAR.

 

USAC Upgrade Points will be awarded for eligible categories and at rates in relation to each category’ length.

 

Wheel Van/Neutral Support: There will be no neutral wheel support.  A follow vehicle will be provided and wheels available on a wheels in-wheels out basis only. Individual team support vehicles are prohibited from the race caravan.

 

Common Courtesy: ABRT would like to remind everyone that we all have a responsibility to leave the race course cleaner than we find it on race day. All refuse should be discarded into appropriate containers. Any rider found illegally discarding objects on the school grounds, the roads leading to and from the race course, and the on the race course itself will be dealt with accordingly (see USCF Rule 3B9, which states in part – ‘Riders may not discard materials that are not biodegradable; they may pass or throw such material to support personnel in places far from any bystanders [relegation or disqualification for littering or unauthorized feeding]). Police, turnaround officials, and corner workers are not ‘support personnel’ and riders should not throw anything to them as they pass. Trash containers will be available for rider’s to use at the school. Please be respectful of the environment and its inhabitants.

 

Sportsmanlike Conduct: The Chief Referee and Race Promoter expect ALL spectators and riders to act like responsible adults. Use of profanity and blatant unsportsmanlike conduct will not be tolerated.

The Midwest Women's Mountain Bike Clinic is more than just a clinic.  It is an entire weekend filled with mountain biking, camping, fun and friends.  Come for the day or stay for the weekend.  We welcome anyone to attend who is interested in learning to mountain bike, whether you are someone who plans to race or someone who just wants to enjoy a day riding in the woods.  Our clinic will teach you the skills you need to feel safe and confident on the trail.
 
Skill levels may vary slightly within each group and adjustments can be made during the clinic to ensure all participants are comfortable and having a good time.  To better assist in selecting a group that fits your current skill level, please see the descriptions below.  
  • Intro ~ This is an introduction to mountain biking.  This group is perfect for the first time rider who has never ridden on a dirt trail.  You may have ridden on paved paths in your local area and would like to give mountain biking a try. 

  • Beginner ~ This group has given mountain biking a try once or twice.  You may have ridden on some dirt paths, but not really experienced more technical obstacles such as log crossings, roots, rocks, etc.

  • Intermediate ~ This group has ridden on various mountain bike trails and able to demonstrate basic shifting and bike handling skills.  You are looking to ride more advanced trails with bigger log crossing and more technical trail features.  Participants should be at a novice to intermediate physical fitness level.

  • Advanced ~ This group is looking for a challenge.  You are a skilled and confident rider who is looking to improve your technique on expert level trails.  Participants must be at an intermediate or above physical fitness level.

Welcome to the 2011 Mid-Atlantic Super Series.  **Important Changes for 2011**

Upgrade Rule - very similar to USA Cycling guidelines

Class winners from the previous year must must move up to the next level. This does not apply to 50/60+ and juniors. These classes will be addressed on a case-by-case basis. In certain cases of small classes certain exceptions might be made. E-mail support@masuperseries.com if you have a question on this. Race results will be closely looked at after the first 3 or 4 races and anyone clearly dominating a class will be required to move up. If the below rules apply to you and you sign up for the incorrect class you will be automatically upgraded.

Beginner Classes - 5 top 3 finishes in the previous year must move up

Sport Classes - 5 top 5 finishes in the previous year must move up

Expert 19-39 Class - 5 top 5 finishes in the previous year must move up to Elite

Class Consolidation - after much discussion it was decided that class consolidation would make for more exciting and competative racing. It will also make it much harder for the same racers to win or place in the top 3 at each race which has always been a problem with smaller classes.
 
Beginner and Sport Men Master II (50-59) and Master III (60+) will race together for the same medals/prizes but will be scored separately for the individual MASS competition.
 
Beginner and Sport Women I (U40) and Women II (40+) will race together for the same medals/prizes but will be scored separately for the individual MASS competition.
 
Beginner Juniors 16 to 18 can still register for the series at no cost by e-mailing us for a coupon code before registering for the series. These juniors are also eligible for the discounted race entry of $10 on-line or on-site. For a coupon code for race registration you can e-mail us as well at support@masuperseries.com

Racers wishing to participate in the series overall individual competition and MASS team competition must register for the series and pay a series fee of $25 for your primary racing class (no charge for juniors) .  Racers wishing to race in more than one class will be able to register for additional classes for an additional fee of $5.00 for each additional class.  For example, if you are going to compete in the XC series competition and the endurance competition you will register for one of the classes and pay $25 and you will add the other class for $5.00.  Another example would be if you intend to race your age class at some races and singlespeed at other races.  Additional XC classes must be within the same XC category (Beginner, Sport or Expert/Elite). No USAC license required for MASS races.  MASS races follow a very generous payout schedule.   For more information visit www.masuperseries.com.
 
Racing Age is defined as the age you will be on December 31, 2011. Make sure you register for the proper class. 
 
For 2011 racers will be issed a permanent number plate with timing chip attached to the back.  If you lose or forget to bring this to a race there will be a $10 replacement charge.
 
Season-end awards ceremonies will take place after the final XC race at the Bear Creek Mountain Resort.  Endurance finals will take place at the Coal Cracker Classic.  Champions jerseys are awarded to every class winner.  Awards are given to the top three in larger classes. Smaller classes will award a champions jersey. Team trophies are awarded to the top three teams in each team division.  

Important - Series registration is only available through BikeReg and will not be available at the races.  You must be registered for the series before a race for points from that race to count towards individual and team points.  There will be no retro-active race credits.

Please indicate which team you are racing for when you register.  However, series team scoring will be based on team rosters submitted by team directors. You must be registerd for the MASS and be on a team roster to score team points.

This is a weather dependent event.  Inclement weather may result in the postponement or cancellation of the race.  If the event is canceled, a notice will be posted on the MASS website and on the BikeReg event no later than 9PM on May 5th and registration fees will be refunded to all preregistered riders.  All Bikereg service charges and fees are nonrefundable.

French Creek is a Pennsylvania State Park.  As such, possessing, selling, or consuming alcoholic beverages is prohibited.   Pets are allowed provided they are on a leash and under the direct physical control of a handler.  If you have any other questions about the rules and regulations of the park, they can be found at the PA Dept of Conservation and Natural Resources website.  Bottom line, use common sense and be a good ambassador of the MASS.  We want to keep racing here.

Unsportsmanlike conduct and volunteer abuse will not be tolerated.  Remember, this is supposed to be fun. 

REGISTRATION AND AWARDS

Preregistration is $30 for the XC and $10 for Juniors.  Portion of the entry fees are given back park for improvements and to the local volunteer groups.  Do us a big favor and save yourself some time and cash by pre-registering. There are 2 ponds and there will be no lifeguard on duty.  Swimming is at your own risk.

However, please be aware that the boats and floating dock are the Oesterlings property and they must be treated with care. Abuse of these items or any other property will not be tolerated.  Destruction of property will result in ejection from the property.

6. Keep it quiet during quiet times. Quiet hours are 11pm - 7am. There will be plenty of time for you to be rowdy and loud cheering on the other racers. Hopefully you'll all lose your voices from cheering and be too tired from racing for this to even be a concern.

7. Don't be a jerk. I'm the only one allowed to be a jerk all weekend since I'll be going on not nearly enough sleep each night and completely stressed about one thing or another. Don't be an ass like me.  If you're a jerk you'll be asked to leave.

8. Respect the property. Seven years in a row you've been perfect ladies and gentlemen and wonderful guests, which is why we're inviting you all back. Please remember that the Oesterlings live here all year long, have been incredibly supportive of mountain biking on this property and are my in-laws so there is no way I can get away from them if you do things to upset them. Well I can, but my wife is pretty great most of the time... Please be respectful of the property and thank the Oesterlings for their hospitality and support of our sport whenever you have the chance.  Hell, bring Rosezelma flowers even!  

9. DO NOT LITTER. I'm not just talking here about the camping area where we will have some trash receptacles, but do not drop your used gel packs on the course. I know you're quite sure that those used foil containers are going to weigh you down and keep you from winning, but if you're caught littering the course you'll be DQ'd (and that don't mean I'm taking you out for a BliZzard). There is no reason to not put that packet back in your jersey pocket or under your leg band 'til the end of the race. The only place you will be allowed to drop the food wrappers is at the start/finish line/feed zone area where they must be picked up by a teammate or your support person.

10. Pack out what you pack in. Going along really well with #8 above. Bring a big ol' trash bag, put your garbage in your big ol' trash bag, put your big ol' trash bag in your car, put your car in your driveway, and put your trash in your trashcan at home. Thanks for helping us keep the place clean. We will have some trash receptacles around the venue, but helping us with little things like this keeps the event going because it keeps me, my crew, my folks, my inlaws, and my wife happy and this only keeps going if we keep smiling!

11. We reserve the right to create and impose further rules throughout the weekend as we deem necessary to reduce inconsiderateness (is that a word?) so that we can all have fun, be happy and get along.

The Bear Creek Challenge is back for the 2nd year.  Once again the BCC has been designated as the Pennsylvania Cross Country Championships by USA Cycling.  We will also once again host the Mid Atlantic Regional Series (MARC) finals.  Anyone racing for the PA States must be a Pennsylvania resident and must have a USAC annual liscense.  All other riders can purchase a USAC day permit.  For more information on USA Cycling, go to www.usacycling.org
 
The big change this year is that we have been designated as a Triple Crown of Cycling event by the US Cup!.  The Triple Crown is a stand alone event with the Short Track and Super D on Saturday and Cross Country race on Sunday. The 3 races making up the Triple Crown. Riders in each class will be awarded points based on finish towards an eventual Triple Crown winner. You do not need a USAC liscense for the Triple Crown. Riders must race in all 3 triple crown races to be eligible for the title.  Scores from your 2 best races will count.  For more information on the Triple Crown go to www.uscup.net
 
The Challenge has been named such for good reason.  Our trails are, well, Challenging!  Lots of single track, rocks, switch backs and a white knuckler downhill!  Our trails are always open so feel free to ride them anytime.  The course will be marked and open for pre-riding after the Super D on 8/13.
 
Bear Creek is a resort with a hotel and 2 restaurants.  Riders will receive a race discount.  Just be sure and mention that you are racing to receive the discount.  So, come on out and be part of a national series in the US Cup or go for that State Championship.
 
Day of Registration is available but will be $10 more!
 
Also, Bear Creek will host a little kids race in the base area so bring the little bikes!

Please join us at Samsung for the 17th annual Rosedale Ride.  

Numbers are funny. One is 1-derful. Three is the charm. Nine is for revolutions, and 11 makes a football team. 16 is, of course, always sweet. But now there's Rosedale Ride 17. Can 17 really be sweeter than 16? Last year's weather was perfect, the roads were smooth, the rest stops friendly and the music toe-tapping, so it's going to be a challenge. But our planning is underway, we're feeling good, and we're hoping to make 17 even better than our most excellent 16. Samsung will, as always, graciously host. The volunteers are psyched. The roads are being checked and rechecked. Even the music is being booked as this is being written. We have a good feeling about 17.

The Rosedale Ride is an annual bike ride benefiting Rosedale School, the Austin Independent School District's only school for children with multiple disabilities. Open to cyclists of all abilities, the ride offers different courses to suit anyone. This year the Rosedale Ride has four courses to choose from: a Kid’s Fun Ride; or courses of 20, 43 or 63 miles. The ride begins and ends at Samsung, winding through the gently rolling countryside east of Austin.

This year, we are making changes to Package Pickup and the Silent Auction.  Put simply, we thought your visit to the School should be more fun. The third Annual BARRY-ROUBAIX March 26th 2011

Barry County Michigan

Presented by KISSCROSS EVENTS

Michigan's 2011 cycling race season kicks off this year with the Killer Gravel Road Race- The third annual Barry-Roubaix! Like the classic it's named after, Barry-Roubaix will test riders against rolling gravel roads (80%), pavement, one mile of rough two track, rocks, sand, mud, and possibly snow and ice, along with 2200 feet of climbing over its 35 mile loop.

What is Barry-Roubaix?

  • A classic road/off road race featuring a variety of terrain and surfaces to test all your cycling skills. Cyclocross, Mountain, Road, Single-Speed, Fixie and Tandem bicycles are all welcome. Road, mountain or cross bikes can be used in any category                 
  • The course will be determined according to conditions just prior to the race start. Maps will be available for pre-riding the course. Click on the map link on the website. The course will have three options and will be marked by colored arrows that match your number plate. Example: 23 milers will follow Blue arrows and 35/65 milers will follow Yellow arrows. (65's must complete 2 laps, not including 2 mile roll in/out). Course marshals will NOT be at every corner or intersection, rules of the road apply!
  • The course will NOT be closed to traffic and does not have a rolling escort. Cycling rules of the road apply, i.e. stop at all stop signs, yield to cars, no more than 2 riders abreast and do not cross yellow center line. Violations will be penalized by disqualification.
  • A sag van will make rounds looking for drop outs.

Where is Barry-Roubaix?

  • City-Middleville, Michigan
  • CourseBarry County
  • Start/Finish/Parking- Gun Lake Unit-Yankee Springs Recreation Area
  • Map: to start/finish area

Who is Barry-Roubaix for?

  • Cyclists and racers of all kinds and performance levels (no license required) that want to start their season with a real challenge and adventure  plus a lot of fun!
    • 65 miles (2 laps)*
    • 35 miles*
    • 23 miles*
    • Single Speed  23 miles or 35 miles*
    • Fixies (one brake mandatory)  23 miles or 35 miles*
    • Tandem- 23 miles or 35 miles*
    • * Distances are approximate depending on final course designation made prior to race start and we reserve the right to combine low category fields.
    • * Road, mountain or cross bikes can be used in any class. The 65 mile race is generally for elite/pro level athletes.  Consider it is March, it may be cold out and last year it took the pros over 3 hours at 20+ mph avg!The 23 and 35 mile races are scored by age, no sport or expert distinction.
    • Cut Off Time: For your safety no individual can start the second lap of the 65 mile race after 12:45 p.m.


What else can I expect at Barry-Roubaix?

  • $2000 cash awards, trophies and medals to the top three 65 Mile racers (no age categories). 1st-$500, 2nd-$300, 3rd-$200.  Michigan Youth Cycling and Kisscross Events will award $250 in scholarship to the fastest under 18 year old male and female in the 23 and 35 mile races each.
  • Trophies to the overall winner of the 35 and 23 mile race. Medals to the top three in age categories (10 year age splits for 23 milers and 5 year splits for 35 milers) and raffle prizes to many lucky racers. Podium awards and photos immediately following the completion of each category.

  • 4 wave starts (one for 65 milers, 2 for 35 milers, 1 for 23 milers)
    • Racers will be disqualified for starting in the wrong wave
  • Chronotrack Timing by Race Services Company. Rigid handlebar number plates with timing chips will be used for the best timing available.
  • All vehicles entering the Gun Lake Unit will need a Michigan State Park motor vehicle passport, either an annual or daily pass for $10. Out of state visitors can purchase a daily for $8 or an annual  for $29. Michigan residents please have permits purchased in advance to speed up the entrance to the parking area come race day.

Sharpen Your Racing Skills for 2011 and Beyond!
 
Join Team Extreme, Tom Schuler and Robbie Ventura on May 13th and 14th, 2011 at the Country Inn and Suites in Germantown, Wisconsin for a world-class two-day clinic and a unique cycling experience.
 
The 2-day camp will be an opportunity to meet other riders, build cohesiveness across teams and help promote safe racing through education. The camp will offer something for racers of all categories and will focus on further developing racing skills, confidence, race strategy and how to win a race through team work  The camp will be lead by two world-class cyclists that now coach or direct teams.
 
Tom Schuler who has been a team director or manager of several professional teams for the past 20 years, including Team Saturn (1991 and 2003) and Team Type 1 (2008-2009). Tom also represented the United States at the 1976 and 1980 Summer Olympics and was one of the original seven members of the 7-Eleven Cycling Team. He won the USPRO National Road Race in 1987 and the US Pro Criterium in 1981. Tom's sports management company, Team Sports Inc. is based in Wauwatosa.

Schuler explains the importance of the camp as follows:  “Strategy and race-day tactics play an important role and the Extreme Racing Clinic really focuses on these subtle elements. We practice then review different techniques and methods of maximizing one's efforts by recreating racing scenarios. Practice, review, repeat is our motto."

We are very lucky to have Robbie Ventura co-leading the camp for a second year on Friday.  Robbie raced professionally for 11 years with his last four years being on Lance Armstrong's US Postal squad. Robbie was a criterium specialist and amassed over 70 victories over his 12 year pro career. Robbie currently owns Vision Quest Coaching and is helping athletes of all levels reach their goals.

“The art of learning to position oneself in a peloton in field sprints is of utmost importance in racing success. Learning how to corner fast and effectively can be a bigger determiner in racing success then absolute power numbers. Everyone will learn how to draft effectively, rotate both single line and double and get the most out of the work of others. At this clinic, we will teach everyone the tricks needed to hold and take a wheel. These are all skills that turn the good biker into a great one.” 

 
 
 
 

The camp is generously sponsored by several companies and there will be plenty of door prizes and product samples for riders.   Each rider will get a clinic t-shirt, water bottle from the Tour of America's Dairyland and product samples from Hammer Nutrition.   In the past, door prizes have included wheelsets, helmets, bike pumps, socks, posters.   This year we are planning on having a shirt or some podium caps signed by Christian Vande Velde, a Kenda Pro Jersey signed by Franike Andreu and several door prizes from Tifosi, Planet Bike, Bontranger, OS Nutrition, Road ID, TheSufferFest.com and more.

The cost for the camp is only $130.00, which includes two days of on the bike instruction, extensive practice drills and classroom talks on training and racing-specific topics.
 

Lunch is included both Friday and Saturday and an all-you-can-eat buffet at La Chimenea Friday evening.   Lots of door prizes will be given away Friday night.  Optional housing for the clinic can be purchased separately at a discounted rate of $89.00 per room at the Country Inn and Suites in Germantown, Wisconsin.   Contact them separately for the reservation and just mention that you are with the Team Extreme Clinic.

details:
Core Skill 1: Body Position and Bike Setup - April 5
Core Skill 2: Vision - April 12

BetterRide head coach Andy will teach you the correct body position for climbing and descending so you can ride in balance, in control and confidently. Then he will help you set up your bike and understand how to make your bike setup work for you instead of against you. Whether you are a pro racer or a beginner this will be an eye opening class as mountain bike skills are not intuitive (like all other sports). Andy will debunk some of the commonly passed on advice and teach you the correct way to ride.

The correct way to ride is in balance, in control and more efficient than other ways that "work" (i.e. I can whack a golf ball all over the course, so my golfing technique "works" but it sure isn't efficient or effective). Andy and I have studied riding technique for over 15 years and nothing we teach did we invent, everything we teach I/and or Andy learned from/with other skilled riders, racers (like World Champions Marla Streb and Greg Minnaar, Ross Schnell), coaches (from many sports, not just mountain biking) and our students.

The following week will be the Vision clinic, where and how to look, how this effects your riding and how to improve your vision, most people know to look ahead but don’t know where and how to look so they end up looking down (go for a ride and note how often you are looking less than 10 feet in front of you), I explain how this effects your riding and how to improve your vision, followed by drills.

This will completely change the way you ride and look at the trail. You will be able to ride faster and in more control while using less effort. (it will also help your skiing, snowboarding, motorcycling, any forward moving sport) Vision is the most important aspect/skill of riding. Most riders know to look ahead but don't know where and/or how to look ahead so they end up looking no more than a couple of feet ahead of their front tire. This makes riding tough, tense and off balance. Learning the proper vision techniques will allow you ride at you best. Without correct vision techniques you will ride at 50% of your ability level or less. I explain how to look ahead (even in the gnarliest rock gardens), where to look and how this effects your riding. I have designed quite a few drills to help you learn the correct vision skills and improve your vision.

We are charging a small fee (compared to our three day camps which sell out months in advance for $499 to $699) to cover my insurance and pay my head coach Andy Winohradsky to coach this.

If you are truly interested in becoming a better rider please come and learn with us. Please bring a functioning bike (clinic time is not time to fix your bike!), an open mind, enough food and water for the evening, helmet, gloves, a big smile and clothing for all weather conditions. In consideration of others please be on time!

Important learning skills

1. Try to look at life with a "Beginner's Mind", with a beginners mindset you are open to all possibilities, with an "expert" mindset your choices are very limited. Think how many "experts" have been wrong, experts once thought the world was flat, and that no one can run a mile in less than four minutes.
2. Get out of the habit of "Negative self-talk" putting your self down does not motivate you nor make you seem modest, it just reinforces a poor self image.
3. Practice makes permanent, not perfect. If you practice a skill incorrectly you will get perfect at doing it wrong. Perfect practice makes perfect. With this in mind we will focus on quality, not quantity when practicing.
4. Knowledge is worthless without action, you must practice and use the tools I give you. Change is up to you, you will get out of my instruction what you put into it. Change requires work!
 
Both clinics will be from 5pm-7pm, the $150 fee is the total price for both clinics.

Core Skill 1: Body Position and Bike Setup
Core Skill 2: Vision

BetterRide certified coach Chip will teach you the correct body position for climbing and descending so you can ride in balance, in control and confidently. Then he will help you set up your bike and understand how to make your bike setup work for you instead of against you. Whether you are a pro racer or a beginner this will be an eye opening class as mountain bike skills are not intuitive (like all other sports). Andy will debunk some of the commonly passed on advice and teach you the correct way to ride.

The correct way to ride is in balance, in control and more efficient than other ways that "work" (i.e. I can whack a golf ball all over the course, so my golfing technique "works" but it sure isn't efficient or effective). Andy and I have studied riding technique for over 15 years and nothing we teach did we invent, everything we teach I/and or Andy learned from/with other skilled riders, racers (like World Champions Marla Streb and Greg Minnaar, Ross Schnell), coaches (from many sports, not just mountain biking) and our students.

After Body Position and Bike Setup will be the Vision clinic, where and how to look, how this effects your riding and how to improve your vision, most people know to look ahead but don’t know where and how to look so they end up looking down (go for a ride and note how often you are looking less than 10 feet in front of you), I explain how this effects your riding and how to improve your vision, followed by drills.

This will completely change the way you ride and look at the trail. You will be able to ride faster and in more control while using less effort. (it will also help your skiing, snowboarding, motorcycling, any forward moving sport) Vision is the most important aspect/skill of riding. Most riders know to look ahead but don't know where and/or how to look ahead so they end up looking no more than a couple of feet ahead of their front tire. This makes riding tough, tense and off balance. Learning the proper vision techniques will allow you ride at you best. Without correct vision techniques you will ride at 50% of your ability level or less. I explain how to look ahead (even in the gnarliest rock gardens), where to look and how this effects your riding. I have designed quite a few drills to help you learn the correct vision skills and improve your vision.

We are charging a small fee (compared to our three day camps which sell out months in advance for $499 to $699) to cover my insurance and pay my head coach Andy Winohradsky to coach this.

If you are truly interested in becoming a better rider please come and learn with us. Please bring a functioning bike (clinic time is not time to fix your bike!), an open mind, enough food and water for the evening, helmet, gloves, a big smile and clothing for all weather conditions. In consideration of others please be on time!

Important learning skills

1. Try to look at life with a "Beginner's Mind", with a beginners mindset you are open to all possibilities, with an "expert" mindset your choices are very limited. Think how many "experts" have been wrong, experts once thought the world was flat, and that no one can run a mile in less than four minutes.
2. Get out of the habit of "Negative self-talk" putting your self down does not motivate you nor make you seem modest, it just reinforces a poor self image.
3. Practice makes permanent, not perfect. If you practice a skill incorrectly you will get perfect at doing it wrong. Perfect practice makes perfect. With this in mind we will focus on quality, not quantity when practicing.
4. Knowledge is worthless without action, you must practice and use the tools I give you. Change is up to you, you will get out of my instruction what you put into it. Change requires work!

Want to have more fun on the trails? Want to be more efficient and mountain bike with more confidence? Still find yourself hoping to make some corners, getting nervous in tight switchbacks or feeling lucky, not skilled after that technical section?  Gene Hamilton and the certified BetterRide coaches know how you feel, because they have all been there.  Gene was held back in his professional racing career by the same fears and lack of proper technique that most riders experience.  But that was before BetterRide…

Gene has designed a comprehensive skills training program that continues to prove itself as the best in the US.  BetterRide coaching sessions will help you with both the mental and physical sides of mountain biking. The goal is to help you reach your potential by teaching you the core skills of mountain biking and the drills to master these skills. These are the non-intuitive skills that keep mountain bikers of all levels from reaching their potential. Learning and becoming proficient at these skills will allow you to ride in balance and in control making you a more efficient and confident rider.

Starting in a safe learning environment BetterRide certified coach Joe will explain then demonstrate the skill and have you practice the skill utilizing drills that you will continue to use long after the camp. Once you understand the skills we then apply them on the trail. At BetterRide Gene and his coaches truly enjoy helping riders progress and would love to share these techniques and the drills for practicing, getting good at and eventually mastering these techniques with you. This is the most fun and informative mountain bike school you will ever attend!

How The Race Works:
The weekly races and overall series are run as a points race, similar to what would normally be run on a velodrome:
  • Riders sprint every 5 laps, with the first 4 riders being awarded points – 5, 3, 2, 1.
  • The middle and final sprint are worth double points – 10, 6, 4, 2.
  • The rider with the most points at the end of the night wins that night.
  • Points are cumulative over the 5 week series; the rider with the most points after 5 weeks wins the series.
  • All riders who register are awarded 2 points weekly.
  • Ties on total points go the rider who scored points latest in the race.
  • The highest points earner who is NOT a Men Category 1-2 rider will win a weekly prize and series prize, but they can only score points by being in the top 4 across the line on sprint laps.
  • The Plus One! race follows the same scoring protocol.

The Tour of the Dragons

Saturday, April 30 & Sunday, May 1, 2011
 Bennington Race Weekend is
Early Season Racing at Its Finest!

The Bennington Race Weekend - The Tour of the Dragons - is a Stage Race of three highly technical, often tough and aggressive courses:

  • a challenging and technical 11.0-mile Individual Time Trial, with varying terrain, some short steep climbs, tight corners and a fast finish
  • a 0.6-mile/lap, lightning fast, technical 4-corner criterium in downtown Bennington. Includes Sprint Competitions.
  • an epic 62.0 mile (97.6 for Men Pro/1/2) point-to-point Road Race with 5 major climbs and a "boulevard" sprint finish. Includes K/QOM and Sprint Competitions.

Your riding venue for the Bennington Race Weekend is nestled between the Taconic and Green Mountains in the Shires of Vermont, a collective of 15 quintessential Vermont towns and villages and a popular four-season destination for those seeking the authentic Vermont experience.

But the scenic mountain terrain is also home to medieval Dragons that lurk in The Shires. Riders must beware as they wind through these beguiling hills.

Can you slay the Dragons? Or just survive them?

COURSE DESCRIPTION

The Bennington Race Weekend Time Trial course is very challenging and technical. Success on the course demands excellent bike handling skills, energy management and gear selection. The constantly changing nature of the course makes settling into a steady rhythm quite difficult but it will reward the rider who is on his or her game. In sections, it is also quite fast. That said, the Time Trial course is quite scenic switching between secluded wooded areas and broad panoramas of the surrounding mountains and farmlands.

START

The race starts on Beech St, just south of (East) Main St in downtown Bennington and approximately 2.6 miles from race registration at the Mt. Anthony Middle School.

The course heads south on Beech St and takes a gentle right merging onto South Stream Rd. At the intersection of Morgan St (to the rider’s right), you will turn left continuing on South Stream Rd. This begins a 1.7-mile gradual climb.


Shortly after the top of this initial climb, the road drops sharply downhill where you have to make a high speed right hand turn onto Maple Grove Rd. If you do not brake for this turn, you will crash.

Climbing out of this corner, Maple Grove levels out for a fast sweeping section past beautiful wetlands followed by a few short climbs. Approximately 5.0 miles into the course, you will crest a hill and descend sharply into a high speed left hand turn onto Strohmaier/Middle Pownal Rd. If you do not brake for this turn, you will crash.

Another series of climbs awaits you before you level out on Strohmaier/Middle Pownal Rd. Shortly after you are fully up to speed, you will approach a 135 degree, hard left hand turn onto Barber Pond Rd. You can not take this turn at full speed.

FINISH

At approximately 7.0 miles you will begin a lightning fast descent on Barber Pond Rd, sweeping to the left and you can carry this speed for another 3/4s of a mile before you begin a stiff climb to the top of Barber Pond Road. Once you crest the hill, you will be able to go flat out for about 2.5 miles before one final climb past Maple Grove Rd (now on your left) and finish approximately 0.3 miles later just before Niles Rd.

Downtown Criterium


COURSE DESCRIPTION

A 4-corner, flat, fast and technical course in the heart of downtown Bennington, Vermont.

START/FINISH

Riders circuit clockwise starting on Main Street just East of School Street. The course begins with a slight uphill before the most difficult corner onto Silver Street. The Silver Street section starts flat and ends in a gentle climb with another technical turn onto Hillside Street. Hillside rolls smooth and flat into a quick descent and wide turn onto South Street, which is a short fast flat leading to turn 4 back onto Main Street and the slight climb.

DISTANCE

0.9 kilometers (0.6 miles) per lap.

Road Race



COURSE DESCRIPTION

The course is a point-to-point race that starts at the Dana Thompson Recreational Park in Manchester and traverses the Shires of Bennington County, including the scenic Vermont towns of Dorset, Pawlet, West Rupert, East Dorset, East Arlington, and Sunderland before returning to Manchester Village.

The course heads north on VT 30 through the Mettawee Valley. Upon entering Pawlet, you will take a sharp left turn, cross a narrow bridge and immediately start a challenging 3-mile climb on a dirt road to the summit of the Col de Rupert.

After descending and joining VT 315 E, you will turn left and begin climbing, gradually at first but then progressively more steeply, to the second K/QOM point at the summit of the Col de Gallop. Exercise caution for serious Shires Dragons!


After a fast descent, a right turn on Dorset West Rd takes you through a beautiful residential area on relatively flat roads. Approximately four miles after turning onto Dorset West Rd, you’ll take a left, then a quick right and another left to begin the moderate climb up the Col de Morse. 

After the descent from the Col de Morse, you'll join VT 7A S, pass through the feed zone, and dive down into the valley on Beech St. which then joins Barnumville Rd. A climb to the east will bring you to the summit of the Col de Mistral and the third K/QOM point of the day. Beware. Dragons!

A sharp right turn at the summit will lead into a fast descent down VT 30/11 S and onto East Manchester Rd., which will join Richville and River Roads that parallel the Battenkill River along the valley floor.

Turn left on Borough Rd, followed by a quick right. There begins the fifth climb of the day to the summit of the Col de North. At the summit the road changes to dirt for about ¾ of a mile, and after it changes back to paved you’ll head south over rolling terrain that parallels the mountain ridges to the east.

At the southern extreme of the course, the road will bend 90 degrees to the right for a descent down into the village of East Arlington. A right turn on Sunderland Hill Rd will head you back north towards Manchester, through a covered bridge followed by a shallow climb. After another short descent, a left, then right turn will bring you out on Rt 7A N.

Turn right and blow it all out for a 4.5 mile burn back to Manchester Village.

Just past the historic Equinox House, a final left turn onto Seminary Ave will offer a ¼-mile, slightly uphill boulevard-style sprint to the finish at Burr & Burton Academy.

Men Pro/1/2 will continue past Seminary Ave., rejoin Rt. 30 N and head back towards Dorset. A right turn for the second ascent of the Col de Morse begins the second pass of the southern loop of this course. The finish will be at Burr & Burton Academy.

157.0 kilometers (97.6 miles) – Men Pro/1/2 only
