Thank you for your interest in the 2011 Killington Stage Race.  We are very pleased to be bringing your the second edition of this legend of New England stage racing once again this year.  For 2011 we are planning to have eight stage race categories and three days of racing.  Based on racer participation and feedback we hope to expand further in 2012!

Stage Racers will receive points in the 2011 NEBRA Ranking System as well as the Cycling Made Real New England Women's Category 3/4 Race Series.

Early registration ends on May 15th.  Entries received after that date will be an additional $20.

Registration closes on May 24, 2011 at 4 PM.

Please note: refunds will NOT be issued if you cannot attend the race.

Circuit:  1.5 kilometers around National Life complex: A 300 meter long downhill, sharp right hander, winding 350 meter uphill section in two steps, and a flat straightaway to the start/finish . Free Lap rule. No neutral support.

Formats:  The C Clinic is an escorted pack ride led by experienced racers to learn cornering and pack skills. The B race is a conventional race for entry level, category IV-V male and women III-IV racers. 

Directions:  Interstate-89 to Montpelier (Exit 8):  Descend onto Route 2, turn right at first light, climb hill and make second left into the National Life parking lot. Registration/start/finish tent is alongside main building.

Registration: at www.bikereg.com or onsite beginning at 10:30 AM - closing 15 min prior to start. 1 day licenses are available to unlicensed B or C race participants for $10. USA Cycling license applications or renewal forms are provided for annual licensees. Refunds only in case of cancellation. Canadian racers with UCI licenses welcome.


Information:  www.onionriverracing.com , or call Mark White: (413)622-9934

Race field limited to 250 riders.
Mass start event with following categories:


Men & Women: 19 & under, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+,
Clydesdale Men 190 lbs+, Filly Women 140 lbs+, Tandem.

Registration and number pick-up open at Jackson Gore Inn, Ice House building on Friday, June 24 5-8PM, day of event at 8 a.m. to 10 a.m.  All competitor parking at lower Jackson Gore Inn parking lots, see signs at arrival and directions below.

Reg fee: $50.00 until 6/1, $65.00 until 6/21. Online registration closes 6/21, $75.00 race morning. Registration for all participants under age of 19 regardless of registration date is $15.00.

Start time is set at 10:30 AM on Saturday June 25th

Organizer reserves the right to break field down into packs for safety and logistical purposes. All participants must wear helmets for this event for both the climb and the descent afterwards.

Bicycles used must be equipped with front and rear brakes and pass safety inspection. Riders will be descending the climb by bicycles at the ends of the event.  NO riders will be allowed to descend the course until course is cleared by race officials. The descent of the course will be behind a race vehicle at a controlled pace.

Course:

The race start location is the parking lot area adjacent to the Spring House building at the Jackson Gore Inn. All riders must be staged and ready to start by 10:15 AM. The race course will follow the Jackson Gore Inn access road down to Vermont Route 103, turning right and traveling 2 miles along Route 103 into the town of Ludlow.

At 2.0 miles you will turn right onto the climb at the intersection of Route 103 and Okemo Ridge Road. At 2.5 miles you will bear left and begin climbing the Mountain Road.  From this point to the top of the climb the road will be closed to all vehicle traffic. The overall distance of the course is 5.8 miles which includes the 2 mile stretch of Route 103 into Ludlow. The climb being 3.8 miles on paved roads the full distance. The climb includes sharp turns and very steep sections. The overall grade is 11% from the 2mile mark to the summit.

Finish location and rules:

ALL riders will be held at the summit until the last rider has completed the climb and/or the course has been cleared by race officials.

NO RIDERS WILL BE ALLOWED TO DESCEND THE COURSE UNTIL THIS TIME!

We will provide transportation of one bag per rider for the purposes of having extra clothing and essentials at the summit upon your arrival. Riders are encouraged to have extra clothing on hand in the event of inclement weather conditions.  Refreshments will be provided at the finish. There is very minimal parking at the finish hence cars may not be taken up to the summit prior to the race.

Spectators may drive as far as the base lodge about  1/3 of the ascent.  Any spectators wishing to observe the race farther up the course must walk or see below.

A SPECTATOR BUS to the finish line that will accommodate the first 26 people that sign up at the registration desk.  Bus will make one trip only and depart at 1000AM, returning immediately after the race.

Upon completion of the event competitors will descend by bicycle and return to the Jackson Gore, Ice House building for post race awards and diner.

The event proceeds benefit the charities of the Rotary International and the Ludlow Rotary Club

RED HOOK CRITERIUM No.4
BROOKLYN 2011

  

Red Hook Crit No.4 Mar 26 2011

       

The Red Hook Criterium is an unsanctioned bicycle race through a desolate post-industrial area of Brook­lyn. Track bikes are mandatory and the field consists of elite level roadies, bike messengers, and urban cyclists. The race distance is 20 laps around a .75 mile circuit which features several hairpin turns, a technical chicane, a cobblestone stretch, and a sprint finish. The Red Hook Criterium has developed a new and unique style of cycling event which combines the underground art of street racing with the intensity of high level com­petition in a fun spectator friendly atmosphere. First held in 2008, the Red Hook Criterium has quickly become established as a prestigious and much-loved event in both the local community and greater cycling world.

All proceeds will benefit the Friends of Wompatuck State Park.

Please note that you save money and time with pre-registration.  Day of registration fees are an additional $5. We will have extra volunteers staffing the pre-registration entries, so it will also save you time on race day, giving you plenty of time to warm up, be indecisive about last minute adjustments to you bike, and to get to the bathroom before there is a line.

First Timers:

This race consists of one 6-mile lap.

 

XC – Cat 3 (Beginner)

As in previous years, Cat 3 racers will complete one 11-mile lap.

 

XC – Cat 2 (Sport) / Cat 1 (Expert) / Pro

Racers in categories 2, 1, and Pro will endure an epic one lap 25-mile course.

 

Marathon

In addition to the XC race, we also offer a marathon category that consists of two laps to make for a 50 mile day of some of the best trails in New England!  There is a $500 cash pot for the Marathon classes.  Riders cannot do both the marathon and the XC race.  We're aiming to have all racers done by 5PM.  This means that if you do not finish your first lap in under 3 hours and 30 minutes, you'll be given a warning, but can continue on.  However, to continue the marathon race, you must make it to Aid Station 2 for the second time (mile 34) by 2:30PM (ride time = 5 hours) to be allowed to finish the race. PLEASE NOTE THAT THE MARATHON RACE STARTS AT 9:30AM.


Start Times

Marathoners have a mass start at 9:30AM.  Everyone else lines up at 10:30AM and will be sent out in waves by class approx. 2 minutes apart.  The waves will follow this pattern: Pro/Open Cat 1 > Cat 1 > Cat 2 > Cat 3 >First Timers.


Kids Race

There will be a kids race at 11:39AM.  This is FREE and all non-motorized bikes are welcome -- training wheels, 16" wheels, or even push bikes.  We will divide the group into two age groups so the younger ones don't get run over.  The course will be open all day and will include some obstacles (log piles, etc.) that your kids can practice on throughout the day.  Helmets are required.  There is no pre-registration for this event -- register day of!  Registration for the kids race opens at 11AM.


Feed Zones

There will be FOUR neutral support feed zones throughout the race. If you plan on leaving your own supplies at these aid stations, you must drop them off and pick them up yourself.  Since you drive by all of the feed zones on your way to the race start area (South Field), it is highly recommended that you drop your stuff on your way in.  Read the directions below and on race day, watch for signs directing you to feed zones once you enter the park.


The first feed zone will be located directly behind the Visitor Center. Since that is only about 5.5 miles (and 30.5 miles for marathoners - though only 5.5 miles from the last feed zone)  into the course, you should probably not put the majority of your items there. This feed zone will only be lightly stocked and water will be available.


The second and third feed zone areas are physically in the same spot because the course runs close together there at mile 9 (and 34) and mile 20 (and 45).  However, they are separated by tape during the race, so if you are leaving drop bags, you will still want to place one at each feed zone. 


Feed zone 2 will be on Union Street on the uphill again this year so that riders are not cranking at full speed in their approach to the feed zone.  Feed zone 3  is located at the two way section near Feed Zone 2. The second / third feed zones can be found about two miles after you enter the park -- you'll see the orange cones and it's on your left.  There will be signs posted indicating where they are. Feed zones 2 & 3 are a short walk from each other.  Both of these feed zones will be fully stocked with items like cookies, peanut butter & jelly sandwiches, Coca Cola, trail mix, etc.


The fourth feed zone will be at the finish area in South Field (the 25 mile mark for marathoners). Look for signs near the registration table. This feed zone will be lightly stocked and water will be available.

Remember, there is no drop service available. You must place your own items at the feed zones.  Make sure you drop off your stuff on the way to the start line so you don't have to back track after registration


Food & Other Family-Friendly Features

A local cub scout troop who uses Wompatuck State Park for many of their activities will be providing the food for this race -- so buy their food and support them!


Also, from 12-2PM Nona's Ice Cream Truck will come to the South Field to delight us with their homemade treats.  This isn't your typical ice cream truck fare, this is excellent, locally made ice cream!


This year, the start of the race will include a prologue lap around the field, so make sure you bring your cowbells to cheer on the racers, or show up early and claim one of the free ones we will be handing out!


The race course ends with a berm in South Field -- so setup there to see how your favorite racers do on it after their long ride in Wompy!


Weather permitting there will also be a bouncy house setup for kids.  Adult supervision is required.


Bridges

If there is one thing unique about Wompatuck, it is the amount of bridges the Friends of Wompatuck has put in and maintains.  There is over 1400 feet of bridges in our park!  In previous years there has been some issue with slick bridges depending on the weather.  We hope to have mitigated that problem this year by spending many of our trail maintenance days resurfacing bridges.  Check out photos from these trail care events to see this improvement.  We hope this will help make you race faster and more enjoyable -- and safer for all.


T-shirts

You know you've seen them around.  The Landmine Classic t-shirts are a racer favorite, though we always seem to run out or don't have your size.  Don't miss out on this year's Landmine Classic t-shirt by purchasing one when you pre-register.  Then you will get the correct size and save some money.  They are only $15!


Course Map

The course map and GPS tracks are available at http://friendsofwompatuck.org/landmine.htm. Please note there will be race day changes to the course. The online map and GPS tracks are an approximation! The course will not be marked until just a few days before the event.

 

Directions
Wompatuck State Park is located near Hingham on Boston's South Shore.

 

From the south and Cape Cod: Rte 3 North to Exit 14 and the intersection with Rte. 228. Follow Rte. 228 North approximately 5 miles to Free Street on the right. Turn right onto Free Street one mile to the park entrance on the right.  Follow the signs to the race course

 

From the North: Follow Rte 3 South to exit 14 and the intersection with Rte. 228. Follow Rte. 228 North approximately 5 miles to the intersection with Free Street on the right. Turn right onto Free St. and follow it one mile to the Park entrance on the right. Follow signs to the race course.


Navigating via GPS?  Type 188 Union Street, Hingham, MA into your GPS and it will get you into the park.  Then follow the signs to the start of the race.  Do not just search for Wompatuck State Park -- it will likely send you to a wrong entrance.


Questions? Contact the 2010 Landmine Classic Race Directors

Mark & Vicki Schow

Event description: The Fifth Annual Leesburg Bakers Dozen is a 13+ hour Mountain Bike Race starting at 9:00am April 9, 2011. This event has been designed to be fun for all racers, family and spectators. Timing will be provided by Go Time Racing using the most current chip timing technology.

We like the feel of the race the way it is and don't want to grow so big as to allow the personal atmosphere of the event to be diminished.

While you are free to register yourself and your teammates, I recommend registering your teammates using their correct information in order to avoid this fee. Captains - Please have your full team information ready when registering.
 
VERY IMPORTANT:  IF YOU ARE SIGNING UP AS A TEAM AND ONE OR MORE OF YOUR TEAMMATES ARE SEASON PASSHOLDERS, PLEASE SIGN UP AS A SOLO RACER AND WE WILL COMBINE YOUR ENTRIES INTO YOUR TEAM AFTER YOUR REGISTRATION IS COMPLETE.  As an FYI, there will be no change fees for this situation.

The SpeedFreaks Stage Race is a 2 day, 3 stage Mountain Bike Race to be held on June 4th and 5th 2011. The event will be held on a private farm overlooking the Potomac River 3.5 miles north of Leesburg Virginia.

 This is a Solo event only and all competitors must complete all 3 races to be eligible for Awards.

 Race Caps: We will be capping the number of registrants for this race. SpeedFreaks will have 250 slots available for purchase, based on a first come, first served basis.

 Race Formats and Course Descriptions

 Time Trial: Saturday Morning. We will be having 2 Time trial courses this year. The Junior and Cat 3 racers will race the same 3.5 mile loop going through the "Pines" section of the course. Racers should anticipate times of 15-20 minutes. The Single Speed, Cat 1, and Cat 2 course will be using the trails on the back portion of the property. This will increase distance, time, and technicality. This will be a ~4.5 mile loop with expected times of 20-30 minutes. Both courses wil lbe running at sdame time, with racers starting every 20-30 seconds. Timing will be done using Go Time Racings RFID chip Timing system, so will be extremely accurate.

 Short Track: – Saturday afternoon. Races all afternoon on a .8 mile short track course laid out in the open so that Spectators can surround the entire course. The track has been layed out to utilyze the rolling hills and rock features of Rockland Farm to create a very fun, fast course. Most likely, Cat 3 and Junior racers will do 8 laps, Cat 2 and Single speeders will do 10 laps, and Cat 1 racers will do 13 laps. Goal is each race lasting about 30-45 minutes.

 Enduro: Sunday 3-5 hour(depending on category) Enduro race using the lengthened Leesburg Bakers Dozen course.The course is made up of rolling hills with plenty of semi-technical challenge in the form of rocks, roots, log piles, and small ledges. This is a fast course, but has been designed to accommodate all skill levels, from Beginner to Expert.

 Please note: The course is located on a private, active farm. The trails are closed to the public aside from race activities. In order to ensure future events and rides, please do not attempt to “poach” the trails prior to or after the event.

 Time Trial - Time Trial races will begin at 8:00am Saturday June 4. Racers will go off every 30 seconds. As we will be running concurrent races, Juniors & Cat 2's will start at 8:00 with alternating starts.  Single speeders, Cat 3's & Cat 1's will follow. Once we see number of entries, we will send out more exact start times.

We are unable to provide exact times until we see how many racers per category we have. Our goal is to have no more than 40 racers in each heat. We may combine categories to accomplish this. The Lake Sylvia Slobberknocker MTB Challenge is an Endurance Mountain Bike race hosted by Central Arkansas Velo (CARVE).  It is Race #3 of the 2011 Arkansas Mountain Bike Marathon Series.  Although it is the least technical of the four races, it contains approximately 7,000 feet of climbing over the 66 mile distance. Lake Sylvia is home to hundreds of miles of Forrest service roads that attract outdoor enthusiast's from far and wide.  A popular destination for Hunting, Fishing, Bird watching, Running, and of course, biking. Lake Sylvia provides breathtaking scenery as well as rolling terrain with a moderate level of technical difficulty.  This event will test your fitness more than your ability to handle your bike on a sketchy trail.  If your goal is a fantastic workout and race experience but you are concerned about the difficult terrain, this event is for you!

Race Bible

And so it has been written, and re-written:

Andrew Mein's Excellent Adventure at Granogue is dedicated to the loving memory of our dear friend Andrew Mein. Andrew was a founder of the Wooden Wheels Mountain bike team, a stalwart in the cycling community, a loving husband, a superb trials rider, capable of amazing flatulence, a terrible bass player, an incredible mechanic, and a very good friend.

Andrew was struck by a car and killed in 1998 while commuting home from work on his favorite bike at the time, a steel fixed gear road bike. Andrew was a hipster 10 years before hipsters knew they were hipsters.

This race is put on not in his memory, but as a celebration of his life, and his vision of mountain bike racing. Andrew believed in fierce and fair competition, and having a great time doing it. Andrew was known for saying, "always be an ambassador for the sport" and for bringing many new racers into the game.  Andrew was a fan of punk rock and the community and grass roots nature that came with it. Please join us in this celebration.


Unsportsmanlike conduct will not be tolerated. Volunteer abuse will not be tolerated.

There is a $10 late fee for day of registration.  $30+$10= $40.  I can hear you now behind the keyboard of your computer:

" $40 !! $$40!! What are you guys trying to get rich? $40 for day of mountain bike registration? I remember when you could buy milk for $1, comic books were a nickel and race entries were $15"

The answer is: yes, we are trying to get rich. In case you haven't noticed promoting bicycle races is incredibly lucrative and secretly paying for Tom, Lauri and my secret vacation home in the south of France. Not really. The house is in Fiji.

Save yourself $10, and make our lives easier go ahead and pre-reg. You know you're coming, you know this is a great race, just do it. Pre Reg. All the cool kids are.

THIS IS A RAIN OR SHINE EVENT. WE HAVE A SPECIAL RAIN DAY COURSE. 

REFUNDS: There are no refunds within two weeks of the event. No exceptions. You can email me, and I will tell you, "I'm sorry we don't offer refunds."

Exception: there are no exceptions.

The course is a classic Northern Delaware mountain bike course. It contains many steep difficult climbs, many technical sections containing roots, rocks, logs, the occasional odd object that may cause a puncture, field climbs, a nasty fire road known as "the koppenberg",  undulating terrain, a tunnel  and many challenging obstacles I cannot possibly explain here. You might be too sexy for your shirt, but let's have a fun day at the race. Oh and If anyone pulls a Baker, and you know punches anyone, we will press charges to the full extent of the law, and you'll be banned from all Granogue events for life.

Why ovarian cancer awareness is important.
  • This year an estimated 25,500 women will be diagnosed with ovarian cancer. 
  • An estimated of 14,500 women will be killed by the disease.   
  • When ovarian cancer is detected early, before it has spread beyond the ovaries, more than 90% of women will survive longer than five years. 
  • Only 24% of women are diagnosed in the early stages.  
  • When ovarian cancer is diagnosed after the disease has spread, the chance of 5 year survival drops to less than 25%. 
  • When a woman is treated by a gynecological-oncologist for ovarian cancer their chances for survival increase tremendously.  
  • Most women are not referred to this specialist. 
  • There is currently no reliable diagnostic test for ovarian cancer.

Don't miss the 2nd Annual MMCC Rust Shaker on April 9, 2011!  Come and and enjoy one of Michigan's newest mountain bike trails on the Harrison campus of Mid Michigan Community College.  It's set in a beautiful forest with massive trees and rolling hills. This trail sports some long, gentle climbs (a few not so gentle) and holds up well to rain. A nice combination of mostly fast flowing trails some tighter technical trails, with a couple short sections of hilly two tracks.  This course will be challenging and fun for all racers.  A portion of the proceeds will go to MMCC student scholarships. 

The Race 
A road rollout that heads into a rolling two track which sets up the 10 miles of single track. One lap around is 11-13 miles.
 
Directions
  From US-127 take Mannsiding Road exit.  Go east on Mannsiding Road, turn left on Clare Avenue (stop sign) and continue 1/2 mile straight to MMCC's main entrance (first right). 
 
Awards and Food
Award presentations and food at 1:00 pm.
Drinks will be provided but alcoholic beverages are not allowed on campus.
 
Great Giveaways
Don't miss your chance to win great swag thanks to our sponsors!
Must be present to win.

Yankee Springs Time Trial
The Devil's Soup Bowl Race 

Don’t miss the largest mountain bike time trial in Michigan:
The 22nd annual Yankee Springs Time Trial on Sunday April 17, 2011! 
This race is an MMBA Western Chapter Benefit event.  Proceeds help the MMBA to build and maintain trails in western Michigan.  For more information, visit www.mmba.org  The course will be challenging and fun for all racers.  Spectators will enjoy the easy access and viewing locations.  We’ll also have a kid’s race and swag to give away.  
 
New in 2011 !!
 
The Yankee Sprigngs Time Trial is race #1 of the MMBA's Championship Point Series.  To collect points in the series you must be an MMBA member and actively register for the series to be tabulated.  New this year, to be tabulated you must go to the Championship Point Series registration here on BikeReg.com.  There is no charge to register for the series and if you are not an MMBA member you can do that on the same registration activity- register for the time trial, MMBA membership and CPS registration all during one visit to here to BikeReg.com
 
Also- the Championship Point Series is supporting the MMBA scholastic biking initiative.  The youth cycling initiative aims to bring more young people to our sport.  In that initiative, you will notice some minor changes to the Yankee Springs race categories for youth- which will be mirrored on the CPS registration as well.

Finally- ELITE WOMEN- returning to the race (and the series) is our Elite Women's category.
 
 The Course
The Deep Lake Trail is fast and flowing in most sections with several technical climbs and descents.  The course is approximately 11 miles long. The trail is 95% single track, but affords enough passing room for courteous racing.  The race is TWO laps for elite and experts and ONE lap for all other categories

 
To get to the Yankee Springs Rec Area Deep Lake Trailhead
From US-131 – Take 129th east (Exit 61) until it becomes Chief Noonday Rd. Turn south on Yankee Springs Rd.  From the east (Hastings, MI) take County Rd 179 (Chief Noonday Rd.) to  Yankee Springs Rd, turn south.
 
Special Kids’s Race
The Western Chapter is proud to once again partner with our youth advocates to promote the participation of young people into the sport of mountainbiking.  See theirg booth to register your young aspiring mountain-biker for the Kid’s Race on a special loop just for the little racers. 
Start-time 1130 a.m.  (tentative).  Awards to all participating youngsters.

Don’t miss the the Fort Custer Stampede on Sunday May 1st, 2011!  This race is an MMBA Southwest Chapter Benefit event.  Proceeds help the MMBA to build and maintain trails in southwest Michigan.  For more information, visit www.bikefortcuster.com.  The course will be challenging and fun for all racers.  Spectators will enjoy the easy access and viewing locations.  We’ll also have a kid’s race and swag to give away.

To get to the Fort Custer Rec Area

The Course
Approximately 9 miles per lap, the race course is 50% singletrack.  There will be plenty of opportunities for passing in the open sections between singletrack.  You'll find the course very scenic and enjoyable rolling through The Trenches, picking veggies in Granny's Garden and challenging through the Amusement Park.  The course is fast rain or shine.  You will not find a finer mountain bike facility in the area!!!!

The Founders Lumberjack 100 also serves as the Michigan Ultra Single Speed Championship!
 
Regsitration opens February 1st, 2011 at 8 p.m. EST...Total field limit is 350 racers, entry fees go up to $160 on April 1st 2011, register early and save!

Entry fee includes one race entry, one staffed aid station, custom Lumberjack technical tee, pint glass, on-site catered meal and Founders Ale at the conclusion of your race.

Awards will take place on site as top finishers in each class complete the race.
 
No refunds of any kind allowed. Transfers will be allowed until June 13th, 2011 but the exchange of the original entry fee is the responsibility of the two parties involved.(additional $20 fee applies via Bike Reg)
 
The procedure for transferring an entry goes like this; the replacement racer goes to the Lumberjack 100 Bike Reg site and clicks on transfers. It will ask his name, address, etc. It will also ask which racer he/she is replacing, the class he/she is signing up for and the original racers confirmation code(sent via email when the original party signed up). It will cost the new racer $20 to complete the transfer. The original entry fee is to be handled separately between the two parties.
 
After I get confirmation that an entry has been transferred I will go into the Bike Reg account and edit the entry so the new racer is a confirmed rider and the original rider is removed. 

NO ON-SITE CAMPING ALLOWED THIS YEAR!
 
Packet Pick-Up will take place Friday June 17th from 3:00pm-8:00pm and Saturday June 18th from 6:00am-6:30am at the Big-M Ski Area Lodge.

The ONE HELENA HUNDRED
A Scenic Century along the Missouri River
 
JULY 16th – 2011
 
Proceeds help support the advancement of cycling in the Helena area

The Helena Bicycle Club invites you to join us on our annual century ride, the One Helena Hundred, on Saturday July 16, 2011.  Riders have their choice of distances - the metric century (100 kilometers/62 miles) or the standard century (100 miles).  Come retrace Lewis and Clark's steps (with a slightly faster mode of transportation!) as they approached the Gates of the Mountains over 200 years ago.

Bicycle from Cascade south toward Wolf Creek and back for the metric century.  Continue from Cascade north to Ulm, heading east toward the Smith River and turning back to Cascade for the standard century.

The route is gentle, meandering alongside the Missouri River with some small rolling hills.  Lunch is provided at Cascade City Park. 


PRE-REGISTER BY JULY 1 --   Preregistration guarantees an insulated water bottle and a pair of custom wool HBC socks.  Note sock size during registration. (socks shown are just examples)





Refreshments and restrooms will be available at 3 rest stops and the lunch stop. Support services are provided for minor mechanical problems along the route.

Be Prepared – Get your bike and body into shape before the ride so you’ll have the most enjoyable time. Plan to carry bike tools, spare tube and pump. Bring your helmet, helmets are required !

  1. Check in – from 7 am and 8 am, at the Cascade City Park – Central and 1st Street

  2. Parking – Please try to car pool if possible as parking is scarce

  3. Directions – On I-15 north of Helena and south of Great Falls take the Cascade Exit (Exit 254 from the south or Exit 256 from the north) proceed into town and turn east on Central (Angus Bar) go 1 block to 1st Street. The park is to the right.

  4. Places to stay – If you are coming from out of town there are many places to stay in Helena.

    1. In Cascade there are a few places stay, check www.cascademontana.com

    2. There are a few fishing access/camping spots along the Recreation Road both north and south of Wolf Creek.

Learn the Skills to Get Faster Guaranteed!  With over 19 years of coaching experience including 12 years coaching downhill mountain biking Gene Hamilton knows how to get you riding at your best.  His coaching highlights include many top pro racers; Chris Van Dine, Mitch Ropelato, Joey Schusler, Eli Krahenbuhl, Chris Canfield, Naish Ulme as well as hundreds of riders and racers of all levels looking to reach their best. 
Dirt Magazine 2009 Pro 4x and Junior Cat 1 Downhill US National Champion Mitch Ropelato in an interview in the October 2009 issue:  
 
Interviewer: “You seem to be able to turn amazingly, what do you put that down to? Got any special tires on there?”

Mitch Ropelato: “Ya, Gene Hamilton is to thank for that, I took his clinic last December in Bootleg Canyon and he was able to show me the correct technique I needed to pull them off.”

 

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

The core fundamental skills of downhill mountain bike racing.  These core skills are not intuitive, unless someone taught you them it is unlikely that would know and understand them. Few US racers know the core skills and even fewer can do them well, which is the main reason we do poorly at the international level.  Through years of coaching and personal experience Gene is able to get the rider to understand these techniques with drills (that you take home with you for further practice and improvement) and then on trail application of the skills.  Get all the details and read student reviews at http://BetterRide.net

This year will mark the 7th year of this increasingly popular event.

 

The Hoosic River Ride is a one-day (rain or shine) event that benefits the education, research and advocacy programs of the non-profit Hoosic River Watershed Association http://www.hoorwa.org. For the last six years riders have responded very positively to the routes, the aid stations, picnic and just about every facet of the event. Locals have loved the challenge of new routes and the novelty of having their workout catered, while visitors have seized upon the cultural opportunities—everything from world class art to great theatre and music, offered by the region—to make the ride part of a great getaway weekend. Again this year the venue will be the Athletic Center of Southern Vermont College, Bennington, Vermont.  Like last year, we will offer four scenic route options that traverse primarily secondary roads with great views, historic landmarks, covered bridges and yes, even a bit of hard-packed dirt (suitable for regular road tires). The routes will be the same as last year with some modification of the 30 mi. Two State Tour.

 

Each group of riders will rollout together to start their chosen route. There will be well-stocked aid stations along the way, and routes will be marked on the road and cue sheets will be available to all. EMT support will be available at all aid stations and back at the registration area. Additionally, roving tech support will exist on each route, although all riders should come prepared with bikes tuned up and ready to go and a spare tube, tire irons and air to support your bike if need be. A complimentary tech check will be available at registration. A wonderful post ride picnic will start at 11:30 and run until 3:00 p.m. to help you celebrate your day.

 

If you register by August 1 you will save $10 on your registration fee. Commemorative ride jerseys are available for $65, or you can raise $250 to get one free, along with a 1-yr. HooRWA membership. We'll try to get an updated image of the jersey up by mid-May.  

 

THE 2011 ROUTES: Named to honor the Ride’s founder and guiding spirit, Lisa Carey-Moore. She and her family have moved to Syracuse, where her husband Justin Moore is now head coach of the Syracuse University crew team.

 

Lisa’s Three Challenge: This 75 mile tour will be the same as last years very popular ride.

This figure eight route (with only 1/5 a mile overlap) challenges the riders with the 4-mile climb up Petersburg starting at mile 48! Tech support will be limited on this ride: come prepared to help yourself (and fellow riders). This route includes a close up look at the Bennington Monument (you'll have the option of stopping here, and taking the elevator up for a fantastic view of the terrain you'll be covering), a roll over four covered bridges (crossing the Hoosic and its tributary, the Walloomsac), a scenic vista look at Mount Greylock, as well as a ton of gorgeous farmland! You'll ascend 4,474 ft, with a few more feet of descent. It’s a challenging ride, but one past years’ riders raved about!

 

The Hoosic 50

It's just that. Also just like the 2010 route. A beautiful ride thru Vermont and New York countryside.  Last year was the first year for this route, but based on feedback from last year’s riders, this will be offered again, and again.

 

The Two State Tour

Stay tuned for more route details; there may be some changes.
